sections.text:
Executing a vision-language-action (VLA) policy involves deciding when to continue an attempt and when to intervene to improve its chances of success. We introduce ACRO, an Actor--Critic rollout orchestration layer that makes these decisions for a fixed VLA.

ACRO seeks interventions that offer a more promising continuation, are physically feasible, and leave sufficient time to complete the task. A Critic learned from policy rollouts estimates success prospects to decide when to intervene and select a re-entry target along the executed trajectory.

Trajectory Retraction shortcuts the visited path to return the robot to that target, where the same VLA resumes execution from a fresh observation. We evaluate ACRO with GR00T N1.7 and $\pi_{0.5}$ across SimplerEnv, RoboCasa, and real-robot manipulation.

Under the same physical execution budget, including all return motion, ACRO improves success by 10.4, 7.3, and 21.7 percentage points, respectively. It also completes additional tasks as the execution budget grows. These results show that controlling when and where a policy resumes can turn its existing capabilities into more successful task executions.

Project page: https://junhoo.me/acro

summary.en: The paper presents ACRO, an Actor-Critic layer that orchestrates execution of a fixed vision-language-action policy by deciding when to intervene and where along the executed trajectory to resume. A critic estimates success prospects from policy rollouts, while trajectory retraction returns the robot to a selected point so the same policy can continue from a fresh observation. The authors evaluate ACRO with GR00T N1.7 and π0.5 in SimplerEnv, RoboCasa, and real-robot manipulation. They report improved success under equal physical execution budgets that include return motion, and additional completed tasks as budgets grow.

sections.text:
Retrieving useful context for a robot requires matching its task, execution stage, and the continuation that should follow. We introduce Robota-Embed, to our knowledge the first vision-language-action (VLA) embedding model to jointly encode all three modalities in both current-state queries and recorded future continuations.

Predictive retrieval training aligns these endpoints, enabling historical continuations to serve as context at inference time. We construct a multi-source corpus of 1,695,684 cleaned training anchors and introduce Robota-Embed-Bench, with 4,000 queries and a shared 8,000-entry gallery.

Robota-Embed achieves 47.33% clip-level and 81.77% episode-level R@1, exceeding action-free Gemini Embedding 2 by 22.09 and 33.47 percentage points. Controlled retrieval studies show that removing native action degrades retrieval more than removing vision. We study two complementary applications.

Embed2ICL uses retrieved experience for training-free and training-based policy conditioning, increasing success from 47.0% to 56.3% in DROID-Sim and from 86.4% to 92.8% on the LIBERO difficult subset, while improving task progress on real robots.

Embed2Evolve uses execution feedback to grow task-local memory and refine context use around a frozen GPT-6 Astra policy. Across five ManiSkill tasks, it achieves 68% success, compared with 24% for GPT-6 Astra Direct and 33% for a harness independently evolved with Omni-Embed-Nemotron-3B under the same protocol.

Relative to the latter, it uses approximately 79.5% fewer policy tokens per test rollout, counting both successes and failures. These results show that a unified, action-aware retrieval space can support robot in-context learning and task-local context evolution.

summary.en: The paper introduces Robota-Embed, which jointly encodes a task, execution stage, and future continuation to retrieve useful robot experience. It describes predictive retrieval training, a training corpus, and a benchmark. The authors report better retrieval results than action-free Gemini Embedding 2 and find that removing action information harms retrieval more than removing vision. Two applications use retrieved experience for policy conditioning and use execution feedback to expand task-local memory and refine context use. The paper reports results on simulated benchmarks, real robots, and five ManiSkill tasks, including success rates and policy-token usage.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Robota-Embed，将任务、执行阶段和后续动作统一编码，用于检索机器人可用的历史经验，并介绍预测式检索训练、训练语料及基准。作者报告该模型在检索指标上超过不含动作的 Gemini Embedding 2，且移除动作对检索的影响大于移除视觉。两个应用分别将检索经验用于策略条件化，以及利用执行反馈扩展任务局部记忆、改进上下文使用。作者在模拟基准、真实机器人及五项 ManiSkill 任务上报告了成功率和策略 token 用量结果。

Simulated environments enable scalable training data generation for embodied agents, but more data does not necessarily provide what a particular agent needs to learn.

Existing environment-generation pipelines largely optimize generic properties such as realism, diversity, or task coverage, while different pretrained policies can fail for different environmental reasons.

We therefore introduce WEDGE, a framework for weakness-guided navigation learning in which the failure modes of a pretrained agent guide the generation of training environments at each adaptation round.

Given a pretrained policy, WEDGE uses an LLM to propose executable weakness features from contrasting successful and failed rollouts, automatically validates them on the diagnostic set, and selects the strongest validated weakness based on its success-rate gap. The validated weaknesses are then mapped to the environmental factors that control them.

WEDGE varies these factors to construct environments in the difficulty regimes where the policy struggles, producing targeted training experience for adaptation. Across three navigation agents with different adaptation mechanisms, we find that policies exhibit distinct weakness profiles and benefit from different training environments.

Weakness-conditioned adaptation consistently outperforms matched random and hard-example alternatives on ProcTHOR, while the resulting gains for Uni-NaVid and Gemini also extend to HM3D after ProcTHOR adaptation.

Iterative re-diagnosis further shows that dominant weaknesses can persist or shift as the policy improves, providing updated guidance for subsequent environment construction.

Together, these results show that policy failures are not only diagnostic signals, but actionable guidance for constructing training environments that target a policy's current weaknesses.

summary.en: The paper introduces WEDGE, which uses differences between successful and failed rollouts to identify and validate weaknesses in pretrained navigation policies, then maps those weaknesses to environmental factors for targeted training. The authors report that weakness-conditioned adaptation outperforms matched random and hard-example alternatives on ProcTHOR. For Uni-NaVid and Gemini, gains after ProcTHOR adaptation also extend to HM3D. Iterative diagnosis indicates that dominant weaknesses may persist or shift as policies improve.

sections.text:
We present LidarVerse, a real-time unified LiDAR world model for sensor simulation across tasks and sensors.

Existing LiDAR simulators largely follow one of two complementary paradigms: reconstruction-based methods preserve the geometry of a captured scene but require lengthy per-scene optimization, whereas generative methods amortize learning across data but lack the consistency needed for long-horizon rollouts.

LidarVerse brings both paradigms into a single, unified conditional generative framework. A universal tokenizer maps LiDAR range sequences into a shared latent space, where a bidirectional teacher learns a common interface for conditioning on a LiDAR prefix, an HD-Map, a persistent spatial cache, and optionally, text.

Varying the available scene evidence turns the same model into a generator of new worlds, a point-cloud forecaster, or a generalizable resimulator of observed scenes without per-scene optimization.

We distill the teacher into a four-step autoregressive causal student and maintain both a rolling temporal K/V cache and a world-aligned spatial cache, enabling persistent long-horizon rollouts with real-time inference at 11 FPS on a single H100 GPU.

LidarVerse achieves state-of-the-art performance on most reported metrics across all three evaluation protocols, while its tokenizer supports 32-, 64-, and 128-beam LiDAR and generalizes to an unseen scanning pattern.

These results demonstrate that generative and reconstruction-grounded LiDAR simulation can be realized within one model, providing the core capabilities for future closed-loop sensor simulation.

summary.en: The paper presents LidarVerse, a unified real-time LiDAR world model for simulation across tasks and sensors. Its shared latent framework combines generative and reconstruction-grounded approaches, supporting new-world generation, point-cloud forecasting, and resimulation of observed scenes without per-scene optimization. The authors distill a teacher into a four-step autoregressive student and use temporal and spatial caches for persistent long-horizon rollouts. They report real-time inference on a single H100 GPU and state-of-the-art results on most reported metrics across three evaluation protocols.
summary.zh: 论文提出 LidarVerse，一个用于多任务、多传感器仿真的实时统一 LiDAR 世界模型。该框架在共享潜在空间中结合生成与重建依据，可根据场景证据生成新世界、预测点云或重仿真观测场景，且无需逐场景优化。作者将教师模型蒸馏为四步自回归学生，并使用时间与空间缓存支持长时序推演；报告称其在单张 H100 GPU 上达到实时推理，并在三种评测协议的大多数已报告指标上取得领先表现。

sections.text:
Embodied visual tracking requires a robot to identify a designated target from visual observations and control its own motion to follow that target through an environment. Following an isolated person is a comparatively simple demonstration of embodied visual tracking, but following the intended person among distractors remains challenging.

Existing methods exhibit a substantial drop in success from single-target to distractor tracking, motivating a focus on the shared spaces that person-following robots must navigate.

We present \method{}, a vision--language waypoint policy built around the hypothesis that visual and language representations should be aligned before tracking-specific motion is learned. The policy combines complementary frozen visual encoders, multiscale temporal context, a transformer backbone, and a lightweight head for robot-centric waypoint prediction.

Its training progresses through vision--language alignment, multimodal reasoning mid-training, and tracking specialization on 19,532 oracle episodes. Compared with 41.54\% distractor-tracking success for our earlier OmTrackVLA model, the complete multi-stage recipe achieves 55.80\%.

We then explore on-policy refinement using filtered oracle labels for states visited by the policy. This preliminary study adds 2.42 percentage points of distractor-tracking success, reaching 58.22\%, while reducing collision rate by 1.99 pts. The final policy records the highest distractor- and ambiguous-tracking success rates among the compared methods.

These results support staged multimodal learning as a promising direction for tracking among distractors and motivate further study of on-policy refinement for person following in shared spaces.

summary.en: The paper presents VLX-Go, a vision-language waypoint policy for following a designated person amid distractors. Its training proceeds through vision-language alignment, multimodal reasoning, and tracking specialization, using frozen visual encoders and temporal context. The authors report 55.80% distractor-tracking success for the full staged recipe, compared with 41.54% for their earlier model. A preliminary on-policy refinement raises success to 58.22% and reduces collision rate by 1.99 percentage points. The authors report the highest distractor and ambiguous tracking success among compared methods.
summary.zh: 论文提出 VLX-Go，一种用于机器人跟随指定人员的视觉语言航点策略，重点应对干扰者场景。方法先进行视觉语言对齐，再开展多模态推理训练和跟踪专项训练，并结合冻结视觉编码器、时序上下文与航点预测。作者报告，完整多阶段训练的干扰者跟踪成功率为55.80%，高于先前模型的41.54%。初步在线策略精炼又提升2.42个百分点至58.22%，碰撞率降低1.99个百分点。结果来自论文所述比较，作者称其在对比方法中取得最高的干扰者及模糊目标跟踪成功率，并将在线精炼定位为初步研究。

sections.text:
Robotic systems that must acquire information about a specific target often face severe occlusion from sur- rounding structures or from the target itself, such that a single camera viewpoint provides only partial information. Active perception must therefore select viewpoints that progressively reveal unobserved regions.

However, conventional local next- best-view (NBV) methods typically select viewpoints according to their immediate utility, which can overlook views that provide limited information initially but enable more informative obser- vations from subsequent viewpoints.

We formulated local target perception as a short-horizon sequential view-planning problem and proposed a Receding-Horizon Next-Best-View (RH-NBV) planner that evaluates candidate sequences of future viewpoints rather than isolated views.

RH-NBV is evaluated on a UR5e manipulator with an eye-in-hand RGB-D camera in simulation as well as on physical robot against a gradient-based NBV planner, and random search, using a coffee mug and Stanford bunny under controlled occlusion and a tomato plant with natural self-occlusion.

Under heavy occlusion, RH-NBV achieves substantially higher target information recovery, reaching 63.8% ROI coverage versus 34.2% and 85.5% occluded-surface recall versus 7.4% for the single-step NBV baselines on the most occluded mug configuration.

A controlled horizon ablation shows that this improvement arises from multi-step reasoning rather than additional computation. RH-NBV provides the greatest benefit for strongly occluded targets, while myopic NBV remains competitive and substantially cheaper when visibility is less constrained.

summary.en: The paper formulates target perception under severe occlusion as short-horizon sequential view planning and proposes RH-NBV, which evaluates sequences of future viewpoints rather than only immediate utility. It evaluates the planner in simulation and on a physical UR5e manipulator with an eye-in-hand RGB-D camera, using a mug, Stanford bunny, and naturally self-occluded tomato plant. On the most occluded mug configuration, the authors report 63.8% ROI coverage and 85.5% occluded-surface recall. A horizon ablation attributes the improvement to multi-step reasoning; cheaper myopic planning remains competitive when visibility is less constrained.
summary.zh: 论文将严重遮挡下的目标感知表述为短时域连续视点规划问题，并提出滚动时域下一最佳视点规划器 RH-NBV，以评估未来视点序列，而非只看单个视点的即时效用。研究在 UR5e 机械臂及腕载 RGB-D 相机上进行仿真和实体机器人评估，使用咖啡杯、Stanford 兔子及存在自然自遮挡的番茄植株。对最严重遮挡的杯子配置，作者报告 ROI 覆盖率为63.8%，遮挡表面召回率为85.5%。时域消融结果支持多步推理是改进来源；遮挡较弱时，较便宜的单步方法仍有竞争力。

sections.text:
Sim-and-real co-training is an effective way to scale robot learning by augmenting limited real-world demonstrations with simulation data. However, existing approaches typically treat simulators as fixed data sources, relying on uniform generation, offline retrieval, or manual parameter alignment by domain experts.

We formulate \textit{Active Generative Simulation}: optimizing a simulator's data-generation distribution to maximize downstream real-world performance.

To solve this problem, we propose MetaGenSim, a meta-learning framework that trains an auxiliary rater network via meta-gradients to automatically discover high-utility data-generation distributions within a user-specified simulation parameter space, without manual parameter alignment.

Across simulation and real-world manipulation tasks, MetaGenSim outperforms uniform generation and retrieval baselines, achieves a 150% relative improvement in real-world full-task success over uniform generation, and matches expert manual alignment.

We further show that distributions curated with a lightweight proxy policy transfer to VLA fine-tuning, and that MetaGenSim can exploit partial alignment through atomic skill stitching and object-receptacle composition when exact sim-and-real task alignment is unavailable. Project website: https://meta-gensim.github.io

summary.en: The paper introduces Active Generative Simulation: optimizing a simulator’s data-generation distribution for downstream real-world performance. MetaGenSim uses meta-gradients to train an auxiliary rater that discovers useful distributions within a user-specified simulation parameter space, without manual parameter alignment. Across simulation and real-world manipulation tasks, the authors report better performance than uniform generation and retrieval baselines, a 150% relative improvement in real-world full-task success over uniform generation, and performance matching expert manual alignment. They also report transfer to VLA fine-tuning and describe skill stitching and object-receptacle composition when exact task alignment is unavailable.

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models provide a promising paradigm for scalable robotic manipulation, yet their reliance on success-only behavioral cloning leaves them brittle; lacking corrective training signals, minor execution errors rapidly compound into unrecoverable, out-of-distribution failures.

To address this limitation, we propose Adaptive Failure-Informed Learning (AFIL), an end-to-end framework that leverages failure trajectories as adaptive negative guidance for diffusion- and flow-based VLA policies.

AFIL uses a pretrained VLA to generate failure rollouts online, avoiding the need for handcrafted failure-mode design or human-in-the-loop recovery.

It then jointly trains Dual Action Generators (DAGs) for successful and failed behaviors while sharing a common vision-language backbone, enabling efficient failure-aware policy learning with limited parameter overhead.

During sampling, the failure generator adaptively steers action generation away from failure-prone regions and toward more reliable success modes, with guidance strength determined by the per-diffusion-step distance between success and failure distributions.

Experiments across in-domain and out-of-domain robotic manipulation tasks, covering both short- and long-horizon settings, show that AFIL consistently improves task success rates and robustness over existing VLA baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness, efficiency, and generality.

summary.en: The paper proposes Adaptive Failure-Informed Learning (AFIL) for vision-language-action policies in robotic manipulation. A pretrained model generates failure rollouts online, which serve as adaptive negative guidance. AFIL jointly trains success and failure action generators that share a vision-language backbone. During sampling, failure guidance steers actions away from failure-prone regions, with strength based on the distance between success and failure distributions at each diffusion step. Experiments across in-domain and out-of-domain, short- and long-horizon tasks report improved success rates and robustness over existing baselines.
summary.zh: 本文提出自适应失败信息学习框架AFIL，面向视觉—语言—动作模型的机器人操作策略。该方法在线生成失败轨迹，将其作为负向引导，并联合训练成功与失败动作生成器，共享视觉—语言骨干网络。采样时，失败生成器依据每个扩散步骤中成功与失败分布的距离，引导动作远离易失败区域。作者报告，在涵盖域内与域外、短期与长期任务的操作实验中，AFIL相较现有基线持续提升任务成功率和鲁棒性。

sections.text:
We present VGM-VS, a visual servoing method built on a pretrained feed-forward visual geometry model. Given the current view and a reference image captured at the target configuration, we estimate the relative camera pose with a visual geometry model and apply it iteratively as the pose increment of a closed-loop pose-based visual servoing (PBVS) scheme.

The geometry-aware representation acquired from large-scale pretraining keeps this estimate reliable when the target is occluded, weakly textured, or covers only a small part of the image.

However, the scale ambiguity inherent to these models leaves the predicted translation defined up to an unknown scale, while the pose increment must be metric for robot control.

We close this gap with a scene-specific metric adaptation: the robot autonomously records image--pose pairs along a predefined motion starting from the target pose, and we fine-tune the camera head on these data, jointly learning the hand--eye transform and thus removing the need for a dedicated calibration process.

We evaluate our method on three real-world assembly tasks with demanding tolerances: USB-C cable picking, cable insertion, and RAM insertion. Running in real time at 30Hz, VGM-VS converges to submillimeter terminal accuracy on the cable tasks, and reaches success rates of 90--100\% when the target is moved during servoing.

It converges in all trials under initial displacements of up to 30cm from the reference pose and with 50\% of the target object occluded, outperforming the compared visual servoing baselines.

summary.en: VGM-VS uses a pretrained feed-forward visual geometry model to estimate relative camera pose between the current view and a target reference image, applying the estimate iteratively in closed-loop pose-based visual servoing. To address translation scale ambiguity, the robot collects image-pose pairs along a predefined motion and fine-tunes the camera head while learning the hand-eye transform. In three real-world assembly tasks, the authors report submillimeter terminal accuracy on cable tasks, 90–100% success when targets move, and convergence in all trials with displacements up to 30 cm and 50% target occlusion.

sections.text:
Differential-algebraic equations (DAEs) arise in power networks, chemical processes, and multibody systems, where algebraic constraints encode physical conservation laws. The safety of such systems is critical, yet safe control is challenging because algebraic constraints restrict allowable state trajectories.

Control barrier functions (CBFs) provide computationally efficient safety filters for ordinary differential equation (ODE) systems. However, existing CBF methods are not directly applicable to DAEs due to potential conflicts between the CBF condition and the constraint manifold.

This paper introduces DAE-aware CBFs that incorporate the differential-algebraic structure through projected vector fields. We derive conditions that ensure forward invariance of safe sets while preserving algebraic constraints and extend the framework to higher-index DAEs.

A systematic verification framework is developed, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for geometric correctness and feasibility of DAE-aware CBFs. For polynomial systems, sum-of-squares certificates are provided, while for nonpolynomial and neural network candidates, satisfiability modulo theories are used for falsification.

The approach is validated on wind turbine and flexible-link manipulator systems.

summary.en: The paper introduces DAE-aware control barrier functions that incorporate projected vector fields to address safety control under algebraic constraints. It derives conditions for forward invariance of safe sets while preserving those constraints and extends the framework to higher-index differential-algebraic equations. A verification framework establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for geometric correctness and feasibility. The authors use sum-of-squares certificates for polynomial systems and satisfiability modulo theories to falsify nonpolynomial and neural-network candidates. They validate the approach on wind turbine and flexible-link manipulator systems.
summary.zh: 本文针对微分—代数系统（DAE）提出纳入投影向量场的控制障碍函数（CBF），以处理代数约束对安全控制的影响。作者推导了在保持代数约束的同时保证安全集正向不变的条件，并将框架扩展至高指数DAE。论文还建立系统化验证框架，为几何正确性和可行性给出充要条件；多项式系统使用平方和证书，非多项式及神经网络候选则通过可满足性模理论进行证伪。该方法在风力涡轮机和柔性连杆机械臂系统上验证。

sections.text:
Perceptive bipedal locomotion over sparse terrain remains a difficult challenge: model-based methods are precise but brittle to uncertainty, while model-free methods are robust but struggle to discover the precise, constrained motions required for safety-critical locomotion where small errors can cause catastrophic failures.

We propose a model-assisted reinforcement learning (RL) framework that combines both perspectives in three steps: （1） generate a safe reference trajectory using simplified models; （2） train a privileged teacher policy guided by a control Lyapunov function (CLF) reward built around the safe reference trajectory; and （3） distill the teacher into a vision-based student policy.

We show that this model-assistance procedure produces physically grounded locomotion, improving sample efficiency, reducing the need for a complex learning curriculum, and achieving smoother locomotion behavior alongside stepping stone performance comparable to model-free baselines.

We validate our approach in simulation and demonstrate successful deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot navigating sparse footholds with lateral constraints.

summary.en: MARCH is a model-assisted reinforcement learning framework for perceptive bipedal locomotion over sparse footholds. It generates a safe reference with simplified models, trains a privileged teacher using a control Lyapunov function reward tied to that reference, and distills the teacher into a vision-based student. The authors report improved sample efficiency, less need for a complex curriculum, smoother locomotion, and stepping-stone performance comparable to model-free baselines. They validate the approach in simulation and demonstrate deployment on a Unitree G1 navigating laterally constrained sparse footholds.

sections.text:
Tiny robots have limited computation and memory, yet visual navigation systems often maintain more state than a task requires. We ask whether persistent memory can instead be shaped by the task. We present \textbf{RingNav}, a \(10.6\)k--parameter visual heading estimator that constrains its memory to the circular manifold \(S^1\).

RingNav learns only the turn between consecutive images, while heading is composed directly on the circle. On the TartanAir Visual SLAM Challenge, RingNav reduces mean absolute turn error by \(27\%\) and accumulated heading error over $4$ sec by \(15\%\) relative to a similarly sized learned-memory model.

The structured update also gives exactly zero turn for identical frames and exact cancellation under sequence reversal. Without fine-tuning, RingNav transfers to real-world drone experiments and continues estimating heading under severe visual degradation.

RingNav runs at $27.3$Hz on Raspberry Pi Zero 2W and can be deployed on an ultra-low power GAP8 processor at $33.4$Hz.

summary.en: RingNav is a visual heading estimator for tiny robots with 10.6k parameters and persistent memory constrained to the circular manifold S¹. It learns only the turn between consecutive images and composes heading directly on the circle. On the TartanAir Visual SLAM Challenge, it reduces mean absolute turn error by 27% and accumulated heading error over four seconds by 15% relative to a similarly sized learned-memory model. Its update yields zero turn for identical frames and exact cancellation under sequence reversal. The authors report transfer to real-world drone experiments without fine-tuning and continued estimation under severe visual degradation.

sections.text:
Reduced-order models (ROMs) make model predictive control (MPC) of high-dimensional nonlinear systems tractable, but the resulting modeling error can lead to constraint violations on the real system.

We introduce CoRE-MPC, a robust MPC formulation that plans with a nonlinear ROM and guarantees recursive feasibility and constraint satisfaction for the full-order system.

It can be applied with a broad class of nonlinear model reduction techniques and the resulting MPC does not require evaluating the full-order model online, thus ensuring computational efficiency. The key insight is in how the ROM affects the dynamics of the prediction error.

We account for this with two error radii that are propagated alongside the ROM and provide a guaranteed bound on the prediction error.

The approach is validated in simulation on an 80-state oscillator chain, a Burgers equation, and a 9,768-state finite-element soft robot, where a two-state ROM with data-driven bounds keeps all 1,628 nodes clear of a wall at a median solve time below 1 ms for a 20 ms control period.

Across these examples, CoRE-MPC is 13 to 61 times faster than full-order robust MPC at only 27 to 35% higher closed-loop cost, whereas existing certified schemes are either infeasible or at least twice as conservative. Code: [released upon publication].

summary.en: CoRE-MPC is a robust model predictive control formulation that plans with a nonlinear reduced-order model while guaranteeing recursive feasibility and constraint satisfaction for the full-order system. It propagates two error radii alongside the reduced model to bound prediction error, without requiring online evaluation of the full-order model. The authors validate it in simulation on an oscillator chain, a Burgers equation, and a finite-element soft robot. In the robot example, a two-state reduction with data-driven bounds keeps all 1,628 nodes clear of a wall. Across examples, they report 13–61 times faster computation than full-order robust MPC, with 27–35% higher closed-loop cost.

items.title: Full-Order Safety for Nonlinear Reduced-Order MPC

sections.text:
Human listeners can often identify the intended object several words before an instruction ends. Robots, however, are typically designed to wait until the speaker has finished before deciding how to act. We present EarlyCommit, an open-source tool that lets a robot commit to the intended object while the instruction is being spoken.

After every recognized word, a fine-tuned text encoder scores each object in the scene. The robot acts when the calibrated probability of the best object reaches a threshold tau set by the user, so 1 - tau is the accepted risk of choosing the wrong object. Otherwise, it waits or asks.

The tool includes a streaming speech front end, a scene and instruction generator with exact word-by-word ground truth, and scripts to train, calibrate, and evaluate.

On instructions containing words never seen in training, EarlyCommit commits correctly 1.6 to 2 times as often as keyword matching, is right at least 92 percent of the time when it commits at tau = 0.9, and needs 31 to 35 ms per word on consumer GPUs.

summary.en: The paper presents EarlyCommit, which scores scene objects after each recognized word and lets a robot act when the calibrated probability of the best object reaches a user-set threshold; otherwise, it waits or asks. The tool includes streaming speech, data generation, training, calibration, and evaluation components. The authors report that on instructions containing unseen training words, it commits correctly 1.6 to 2 times as often as keyword matching. At a threshold of 0.9, committed choices are at least 92% correct, with 31 to 35 ms processing per word on consumer GPUs.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 EarlyCommit，使机器人能在用户逐词说出指令时判断目标物体，并在校准后的最佳目标概率达到用户设定阈值时执行，否则等待或询问。系统包含流式语音前端、场景与指令生成器，以及训练、校准和评估脚本。作者报告，在含训练中未见词语的指令上，该方法正确提交的次数是关键词匹配的1.6至2倍；阈值为0.9时，提交判断的正确率至少为92%，消费级 GPU 上每词处理需31至35毫秒。

items.title: EarlyCommit: Calibrated Word-by-Word Commitment for Robots Acting Before You Finish Speaking

sections.text:
Virtual reality training for robot-assisted vascular intervention requires accurate robotic control and effective feedback on guidewire--vessel interactions. This paper presents a VR training system combining asynchronous dual-mode command mapping with sensorless interaction estimation.

The system supports velocity-controlled navigation and position-driven incremental manipulation. Guidewire deformation and a Hunt--Crossley-type contact response are combined and temporally filtered to estimate interaction intensity, while trajectory-based visualization supports post-procedure review.

Tests confirmed distinct command-dispatch patterns across three velocity gears and the position mode. During hybrid-scene navigation, the estimated response remained low during straight insertion and increased as the guidewire bent within the vascular model.

Trajectory analysis yielded a model-derived cumulative trauma work (CTW) value of 15.166 in normalized units and localized regions of elevated interaction. In a preliminary study with 15 novices, physical-phantom task success increased from 53.3% to 93.3% after VR training, while mean completion time decreased from 132.4 s to 96.7 s.

These results demonstrate the system's dual-mode operation, deformation-sensitive feedback, and potential to improve subsequent physical-phantom task performance.

summary.en: The paper presents a virtual reality training system for robot-assisted vascular intervention. It combines asynchronous dual-mode control with sensorless estimates of guidewire interaction, using deformation, a contact response model, and temporal filtering. Tests showed distinct command patterns for velocity gears and position control, and estimated interaction rose when the guidewire bent in a hybrid scene. In a preliminary study of 15 novices, physical-phantom task success increased after VR training while mean completion time decreased. The authors describe the results as evidence of system operation and potential to improve subsequent phantom performance.
summary.zh: 论文提出用于机器人辅助血管介入的虚拟现实训练系统，结合异步双模式控制和无传感器交互估计，支持速度控制导航及位置驱动的增量操作。系统通过导丝形变、接触响应和时间滤波估计交互强度，并以轨迹可视化辅助术后回顾。测试显示，不同速度档和位置模式具有不同指令分发模式；混合场景中，直线插入时估计响应较低，导丝弯曲时响应上升。15名新手的初步研究中，虚拟训练后实体模型任务成功率上升，平均完成时间下降。作者称这些结果显示系统功能及改善后续实体模型任务表现的潜力。

items.title: A VR Training System for Robot-Assisted Vascular Intervention with Dual-Mode Control and Model-Based Interaction Response

sections.text:
Training vision-language-action (VLA) policies for humanoid loco-manipulation is constrained by the high cost and complexity of collecting human teleoperation demonstrations. VLA policies fine-tuned in simulators have so far transferred poorly to humanoid loco-manipulation tasks.

We present LEGS (Loco-manipulation via Embodied Gaussian Splatting), a hybrid simulator that composites a mesh foreground (robot, objects, props) over a photorealistic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) background reconstructed from a handheld scene capture.

LEGS uses a procedural motion-primitive generator to synthesize labeled demonstrations at scale without human teleoperation, and a two-stage color calibration that aligns renders to the deployment camera.

On a Unitree G1 humanoid robot, across three pick-and-place tasks of increasing whole-body difficulty and three VLA backbones ($\psi_0$, $\pi_{0.5}$, GR00T N1.6), a policy trained purely on LEGS data matches or exceeds one trained on human teleoperation demos on every experiment.

It also outperforms a mesh-only baseline trained on the same motions without the calibrated 3DGS frontend. Because motion is recorded independently of appearance, the same demonstrations can be re-rendered for a target scene and objects at over 15x lower cost than teleoperation.

When both the objects and the scene change, a policy trained on LEGS-AUG data re-rendered for that target maintains task success, while the teleop baseline fails entirely. Code and videos are available at https://hojjunekim.github.io/legs/.

summary.en: LEGS is a hybrid simulator that combines a mesh foreground containing the robot and objects with a photorealistic 3D Gaussian Splatting background reconstructed from handheld scene capture. It generates labeled demonstrations through procedural motion primitives without human teleoperation and calibrates colors to the deployment camera. On a Unitree G1 across three pick-and-place tasks and three VLA backbones, the authors report that policies trained only on LEGS data matched or exceeded human-teleoperation policies in every experiment and outperformed a mesh-only baseline. With both scene and objects changed, LEGS-AUG maintained task success while the teleoperation baseline failed.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 LEGS，一种将机器人、物体和道具的网格前景与由手持场景采集重建的高真实感 3D 高斯泼溅背景组合的混合模拟器。它通过程序化运动原语生成无需人工遥操作的标注示范，并进行两阶段颜色校准以匹配部署相机。在 Unitree G1 上针对三项难度递增的取放任务和三种 VLA 骨干网络，作者报告仅用 LEGS 数据训练的策略在每项实验中达到或超过人工遥操作示范训练策略，也优于未校准 3DGS 前端的网格基线。场景和物体同时变化时，LEGS-AUG 策略保持任务成功，而遥操作基线完全失败。

items.title: LEGS: Fine-Tuning Teleop-Free VLAs for Humanoid Loco-manipulation in an Embodied Gaussian Splatting World

sections.text:
Robot actions vary in both extent and mode: how much change they produce and what kind of change they produce. A latent action space that reflects this structure may make it easier for downstream policies to map latent actions to robot actions.

However, existing latent action methods typically rely on visual reconstruction from observation pairs without explicitly encouraging such structure.

We introduce Polar Latent Actions with Radial structure (PoLAR), which imposes a radial-direction structure on latent actions, encouraging radius to encode transition extent and direction to retain transition mode.

PoLAR uses temporal offsets between observations as a weak proxy for transition extent, encouraging transitions with larger offsets to occupy larger radii. We instantiate this structure in hyperbolic space, whose expanding volume with radius offers a natural fit for more diverse transition modes at larger extents.

Across in-task and large-scale pretraining settings, PoLAR improves downstream policy performance in simulation and real-world robot experiments, outperforming latent action baselines and strong pretrained VLAs. These results suggest that structuring latent actions by extent and mode helps transfer visual pretraining to robot policy learning.

summary.en: The paper introduces PoLAR, a latent action representation that associates transition extent with radius and transition mode with direction. It uses temporal offsets between observations as a weak proxy for extent, encouraging larger-offset transitions to occupy larger radii, and instantiates the structure in hyperbolic space. The authors report improved downstream policy performance in both in-task and large-scale pretraining settings, in simulation and real-world robot experiments, compared with latent action baselines and strong pretrained VLAs. They conclude that organizing latent actions by extent and mode helps transfer visual pretraining to robot policy learning.
summary.zh: 论文提出 PoLAR，一种为机器人策略学习设计的潜在动作表示，将动作变化幅度与变化模式分别关联到潜在空间的半径和方向。该方法利用观测之间的时间偏移作为变化幅度的弱代理，鼓励偏移较大的转移具有更大的半径，并在双曲空间中实现这种结构，以容纳较大幅度下更多样的模式。作者报告，在任务内和大规模预训练设置中，PoLAR 在仿真及真实机器人实验的下游策略表现优于潜在动作基线和强预训练 VLA。结果表明，按幅度和模式组织潜在动作有助于视觉预训练向机器人策略学习迁移。

items.title: PoLAR: Factorizing Extent and Mode in Latent Actions for Robot Policy Learning

sections.text:
Instruction-Conditioned Motion Control (ICMC) separates parameter specification, instruction generation, and code synthesis for language-driven robot control, making execution outcomes traceable to instructions and programs.

We compare one-shot generation with ICMC under o1 and o4-mini on cube pick-and-place and letter-reshaping tasks for a UR5e arm in MuJoCo. We then train an open-weight instruction policy by GRPO through a frozen code generator on cube placement onto two- and five-cube letter layouts, averaging the rewards of five programs per instruction.

The logged positive-reward rate rose from 31.6% to 35.3% (253/800 to 282/800) between the first and last five training steps. A log audit identifies positive binary labels associated with geometric-failure messages: at least 19 in that run, 18 in the dense-reward run, and 5 in the run with one program per instruction.

In one case, all five rewards were 1.0 while the log reports a 0.9515 m miss against a 0.05 m tolerance; the verdict came from the program's own output stream. We distinguish logged reward rates from independently verified task success and report descriptive results for each configuration's single training trajectory.

We introduce an independent evaluation protocol that checks task completion against fixed specifications, separating robot control from success assessment to support reproducible evaluation.

summary.en: The paper introduces Instruction-Conditioned Motion Control, which separates language-driven robot control into parameter specification, instruction generation, and code synthesis. It compares this approach with one-shot generation on UR5e tasks in MuJoCo and trains an instruction policy through a frozen code generator. The reported increase in logged positive rewards comes from a single training trajectory; the authors also identify positive labels associated with geometric failures. They distinguish these logged rates from independently verified task success and propose an evaluation protocol based on fixed specifications.
summary.zh: 论文提出指令条件运动控制（ICMC），将语言驱动的机器人控制拆分为参数指定、指令生成和代码合成，并比较其与一次性生成在 MuJoCo 中 UR5e 机械臂任务上的表现。作者还通过冻结的代码生成器训练指令策略，报告单条训练轨迹中日志正奖励率的变化，同时指出日志存在将几何失败标为正奖励的情况。因此，日志奖励率不等同于独立验证的任务成功率。论文提出按固定规格独立检查任务完成情况的评估协议。

items.title: Instruction-Conditioned Motion Control for Robotic Arms: Language-to-Code Decomposition and Reinforcement Learning

sections.text:
Long-horizon precise manipulation produces mixed-quality data for post-training vision-language-action (VLA) models: even successful demonstrations and intervention-assisted rollouts may contain detours, hesitations, failed attempts, and imperfect recoveries.

The key challenge is to identify which action chunks actually advance the task, rather than uniformly cloning or discarding imperfect trajectories.

We propose Graph-Reweighted Behavior Cloning (GR-BC), an offline iterative post-training framework that builds a task-conditioned goal-reachability graph over demonstrations and iteratively collected rollouts, including both successful and failed episodes with human interventions.

Reverse graph search computes minimal remaining steps to task success within the dataset support, and each action chunk is weighted by how much its execution reduces this potential.

This consequence-based weighting reuses recoverable segments from failed trajectories, leverages interventions as recovery paths, and down-weights locally regressive chunks even inside successful trajectories.

New rollouts are incorporated by appending them to the graph and rerunning search, without training a reward model, action-conditioned critic, or progress predictor.

Across four precise manipulation tasks and three VLA backbones, GR-BC improves single-round supervised fine-tuning and reaches 91% success after a few offline iterations, without trajectory comparisons or progress labels. More details and videos are available at: https://gr-bc.github.io

summary.en: The paper proposes Graph-Reweighted Behavior Cloning (GR-BC), an offline iterative post-training framework for vision-language-action models. It builds a task-conditioned goal-reachability graph from demonstrations and rollouts, including failed episodes with human interventions. Reverse search estimates the minimum remaining steps to success within the dataset, and action chunks are weighted by how much they reduce that distance. This can reuse recoverable segments while down-weighting regressive actions. The authors report improved single-round fine-tuning and 91% success after a few offline iterations across four manipulation tasks and three VLA backbones.
summary.zh: 论文提出离线迭代后训练框架 GR-BC，用任务条件下的目标可达图分析演示数据及包含人工干预的成功和失败轨迹。反向图搜索计算数据支持范围内到达成功所需的最少步数，并依据动作片段降低剩余步数的程度赋权，以利用失败轨迹中的可恢复片段和干预恢复路径，同时降低局部倒退动作的权重。新轨迹可加入图中并重新搜索，无需训练奖励模型或进度预测器。作者报告，该方法在四项精细操作任务和三种 VLA 主干上提升单轮微调表现，并经数轮离线迭代达到 91% 成功率。

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models have rapidly advanced generalist robot manipulation by harnessing the semantic knowledge of pretrained vision-language backbones. However, their visual representations are typically grounded in 2D image coordinates rather than calibrated camera geometry.

This limitation is especially pronounced in multi-camera systems, where views are coupled by known intrinsics and extrinsics but processed as independent images.

We propose G$^3$VLA, a camera-aware geometric module that injects calibrated structure into the visual-token stream of a pretrained VLA without altering its action space or original action-learning objective.

G$^3$VLA combines intrinsic-conditioned ray embeddings, projective positional encoding (PRoPE), and bidirectional cross-view fusion to establish geometrically consistent representations across camera views.

Geometric supervision is provided by ground-truth point maps or confidence-gated $\pi^3$X teacher predictions, enabling training without depth sensors or manual geometric annotations.

On $\pi_0$, G$^3$VLA consistently improves performance on LIBERO and RoboCasa24 under both supervision regimes, while ground-truth supervision improves five-task RoboTwin2.0 averages with three cameras. Experiments on camera-shifted LIBERO-Goal and real robots demonstrate improved robustness to unseen camera viewpoints.

Controlled calibration studies across $\pi_0$ and $\pi_{0.5}$ show that these gains depend on correct camera geometry while remaining stable under mild calibration perturbations.

These results demonstrate that grounding VLA visual tokens in calibrated camera geometry provides a simple and general mechanism for improving geometric consistency, multi-view reasoning, and viewpoint robustness in pretrained robot policies.

summary.en: The paper proposes G³VLA, a camera-aware module that adds calibrated geometry to visual tokens in pretrained vision-language-action models without changing the action space or original learning objective. It combines intrinsic-conditioned ray embeddings, projective positional encoding, and bidirectional cross-view fusion. Geometric supervision comes from point maps or confidence-gated teacher predictions. The authors report improvements on LIBERO and RoboCasa24 for π₀ under both supervision regimes, and on RoboTwin2.0 with three cameras under ground-truth supervision. Camera-shift and calibration studies indicate robustness to unseen viewpoints and dependence on correct camera geometry.
summary.zh: 论文提出 G³VLA，一种将标定相机几何信息注入预训练视觉语言动作模型视觉 token 的模块，不改变其动作空间或原有动作学习目标。该方法结合内参条件射线嵌入、投影位置编码和双向跨视角融合，并以真实点图或置信度门控的教师预测提供几何监督。作者报告，在不同监督设置下，该方法提升了 π₀ 在 LIBERO 和 RoboCasa24 上的表现；真实点图监督也提升了三摄像头 RoboTwin2.0 五任务平均成绩。相机视角变化及标定实验显示其对未见视角的鲁棒性，以及增益对正确几何信息的依赖。

items.title: G$^3$VLA: Geometric Inductive Bias for Vision-Language-Action Models

sections.text:
Whole-body control plays a crucial role in enabling humanoid robots to execute expressive motions. Faithful execution requires preserving both the intended action and its expressive characteristics.

Existing whole-body trackers typically balance joint and keypoint tracking with physical stability across diverse motions, but these objectives do not necessarily prioritize the expressive characteristics of each action.

Our analysis shows that lower average positional tracking error does not guarantee better preservation of dynamic and postural motion characteristics. To address this gap, we propose a residual learning framework with compensation objectives targeting amplitude, energy, body expansion, body lean, and pelvis height.

To concentrate compensation while limiting interference with the underlying tracking behavior, motion-aware gating allocates correction capacity according to body-part activity, preserving larger correction ranges in more active parts and restricting them elsewhere.

For each frozen tracker, we train motion-specific residual policies and distill them into a unified policy shared across motion categories. Simulation and physical experiments on the Unitree G1 across eight motion categories demonstrate superior preservation of dynamic and postural motion characteristics compared with the corresponding baselines.

summary.en: The paper proposes a residual-learning framework for humanoid whole-body control that aims to preserve the dynamic and postural characteristics of expressive motions. Its compensation objectives cover amplitude, energy, body expansion, body lean, and pelvis height. Motion-aware gating allocates correction capacity by body-part activity to limit interference with the underlying tracker. The authors train motion-specific residual policies for frozen trackers and distill them into one policy shared across motion categories. Simulation and physical experiments on Unitree G1 cover eight categories; the authors report better preservation than corresponding baselines.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种残差学习框架，旨在让人形机器人全身控制在跟踪动作时保留动作的动态和姿态表达特征。补偿目标包括动作幅度、能量、身体舒展度、躯干倾斜和骨盆高度；运动感知门控按身体部位活动程度分配修正能力，以减少对原跟踪行为的干扰。作者为冻结的跟踪器训练动作专用残差策略，再将其蒸馏为跨动作类别的统一策略。仿真和 Unitree G1 实物实验覆盖八类动作，作者称该方法比相应基线更能保留这些特征。

Robots following persistent language instructions must decide which cached room judgments remain valid as their environment changes. We present MIND (Maintenance via INstruction-conditioned Dependencies), a framework for maintaining target-room decisions without re-evaluating every room after each event.

A language model compiles each instruction into dependencies for semantic qualification and target selection. The controller intersects semantic dependencies with event footprints, refreshes affected judgments, and updates reachability and selection separately.

For fixed deterministic evaluation, planning, and selection, conservative dependency and footprint coverage preserves the decisions of full recomputation. On 240 five-event ProcTHOR sequences with an exact benchmark predicate, MIND reduces mean semantic evaluations from 30.6 to 11.2 while preserving all 1,200 post-event decisions.

Frozen-evaluator experiments with Phi-4 and Qwen3-14B also preserve all 1,200 decisions, without improving the evaluators' underlying task accuracy. In 32 closed-loop AI2-THOR episodes using exact-predicate qualification and metadata-derived footprints, MIND matches the final target decision of full recomputation in every episode.

Unitree G1 experiments demonstrate target reuse and reselection across room transitions without additional semantic evaluations under MIND, and abstention after a barrier and an object removal at 4 evaluations against 15 to 18.Additional materials are available at https://mind-icra27.github.io/.

summary.en: The paper presents MIND, a framework for maintaining target-room judgments under persistent language instructions as environments change, without reassessing every room after each event. A language model compiles instructions into dependencies for semantic qualification and target selection; the controller refreshes affected judgments based on event footprints and updates reachability and selection separately. Under fixed deterministic evaluation, planning, and selection, the authors say conservative coverage preserves full-recomputation decisions. They report preserved decisions in ProcTHOR sequences, frozen-evaluator tests, and closed-loop AI2-THOR episodes. Unitree G1 experiments demonstrate target reuse, reselection, and abstention after environmental changes.

sections.text:
Reinforcement learning has enabled robust locomotion for legged robots, but learned policies are typically tied to a specific robot morphology and require additional engineering when the number of legs, actuators, or mechanical properties change.

We present PolyMorph, a morphology-conditioned framework that learns a single locomotion policy for heterogeneous legged robots. PolyMorph converts each robot's URDF into joint-link modules and combines a recurrent encoder, graph-based Transformer, and per-joint decoder to generate actions across variable leg counts and joint configurations.

To improve training stability, PolyMorph uses morphology-normalized rewards, adaptive robot sampling, and URDF-derived PD-gain initialization.

We evaluate PolyMorph in simulation across bipedal, tripedal, and quadrupedal robots, including unseen morphology variants and platforms, and deploy the policy on real quadruped platforms operated in multiple configurations. The results show that a single PolyMorph policy generalizes across diverse robot morphologies without per-robot policy retraining.

summary.en: The paper introduces PolyMorph, a morphology-conditioned framework for learning one locomotion policy across heterogeneous legged robots. It converts each robot's URDF into joint-link modules and combines a recurrent encoder, graph-based Transformer, and per-joint decoder to handle varying leg counts and joint configurations. Training uses morphology-normalized rewards, adaptive robot sampling, and URDF-derived PD-gain initialization. Simulation evaluations cover bipedal, tripedal, and quadrupedal robots, including unseen variants and platforms. The authors also deploy the policy on real quadruped platforms in multiple configurations and report generalization across morphologies without per-robot policy retraining.
summary.zh: 论文提出 PolyMorph，一种形态条件化框架，目标是让异构足式机器人共用一个运动策略。系统将机器人的 URDF 转换为关节—连杆模块，并结合循环编码器、基于图的 Transformer 和逐关节解码器，以适配不同腿数和关节配置。为提高训练稳定性，方法采用形态归一化奖励、自适应机器人采样及基于 URDF 的 PD 增益初始化。仿真评估涵盖双足、三足和四足机器人及未见形态变体与平台；作者还在多种配置的真实四足平台上部署策略，并报告无需按机器人重新训练即可跨形态泛化。

It has been difficult to accurately model the physics of the interaction between a robot and the objects it manipulates, including contact mechanics, coupled contact dynamics, deformations, stiffness and friction.

We present RoboSimStudio (RSS), an interactive toolkit that makes choices of solver, contact model, and physical parameters explicit and editable, allowing both humans and coding agents to quickly create and iteratively refine simulations based on observed physical behavior.

We implement RSS with the open Newton physics simulation system and describe experiments with human-guided real2sim using （1） visual evaluation, （2） force-feedback and （3） agentic Real2Sim2Real. Code, video and additional information can be found on the project website: https://robosimstudio.github.io

summary.en: The paper introduces RoboSimStudio (RSS), an interactive toolkit for rapidly creating and refining simulations of robot manipulation tasks. It addresses challenges in modeling contact mechanics, coupled contact dynamics, deformation, stiffness, and friction. RSS makes the choice of solver, contact model, and physical parameters explicit and editable, enabling humans and coding agents to iteratively build simulations based on observed physical behavior. The toolkit is implemented with the open Newton physics simulation system. The authors describe human-guided real2sim experiments involving visual evaluation, force feedback, and agentic Real2Sim2Real; the abstract does not state their results.

sections.text:
Image-goal navigation requires a global planner that connects visually specified endpoints while providing observations that a local policy can follow. Three-dimensional Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides map-registered RGB, opacity, and depth renderings, but does not explicitly encode navigable topology.

We introduce \method, a Gaussian visual roadmap whose milestones, local connections, and visual references are constructed directly through 3DGS rendering without deriving an occupancy grid or signed distance field. We define render-based collision-free (RC-free) configurations and paths.

Panoramic depth supplies conservative clearance for milestone validation and adaptive coverage, while edge-aligned orthographic rendering tests the robot's swept volume. We establish conditional soundness and sufficient conditions for deterministic query completeness and probabilistic construction completeness of GS-PRM.

To validate the performance of GS-PRM, we conduct experiments in both simulated and real-world environments, demonstrating long-horizon navigation using goal-conditioned policies guided by GS-PRM.

Compared with a state-of-the-art 3DGS-based navigation system, our GS-PRM-based navigation system achieves up to a twice higher average success rate and reduces travel time by up to 57.2% when both systems complete the navigation task.

summary.en: The paper introduces GS-PRM, a Gaussian visual roadmap built directly through 3D Gaussian Splatting renderings, without first deriving an occupancy grid or signed distance field. Panoramic depth supports milestone validation and conservative clearance estimates, while edge-aligned orthographic renderings test the robot’s swept volume. The authors establish conditional soundness and sufficient conditions for deterministic query and probabilistic construction completeness. Simulated and real-world experiments demonstrate long-horizon navigation guided by goal-conditioned policies. Against a state-of-the-art 3DGS navigation system, the authors report up to twice the average success rate and up to 57.2% less travel time when both systems complete the task.
summary.zh: 论文提出 GS-PRM，一种直接利用三维高斯泼溅渲染构建的高斯视觉路线图，无需先生成占据栅格或有符号距离场。该方法以全景深度验证路标并估计保守间隙，以边缘对齐的正交渲染检测机器人扫掠体积；作者给出条件安全性及确定性查询完备性、概率构建完备性的充分条件。仿真和真实环境实验展示了其引导目标条件策略进行长时程导航的能力。与一种先进的三维高斯导航系统相比，作者报告称，在两系统均完成任务时，平均成功率最高提高一倍，行程时间最多减少57.2%。

sections.text:
Recent advances in reinforcement learning (RL) have demonstrated impressive whole-body agility for humanoid robots, yet ensuring safety and satisfying constraints -- particularly those specified after training -- remains a challenge.

Towards this goal, we present ConstrainedMimic, a control framework that leverages whole-body kinematics and dynamics for real-time constraint enforcement within RL tracking policies.

By integrating principles from operational space control and control barrier functions, we enable the satisfaction of arbitrary runtime constraints on both the kinematic reference motion and the underlying dynamics, with efficient computation at frequencies above 1 kHz.

In whole-body motion-tracking experiments in simulation and hardware, we demonstrate collision avoidance (both with the robot body and external obstacles), joint limits, and center of mass stability constraints.

By remaining consistent with the current contact mode and tracking objectives, we minimally restrict the capabilities of the policy when constraints are active. Project page: https://stanfordasl.github.io/constrainedmimic.

summary.en: The paper presents ConstrainedMimic, a framework for enforcing constraints in real time within reinforcement-learning tracking policies for humanoid robots. It combines whole-body kinematics and dynamics with operational-space control and control barrier functions to impose runtime constraints on reference motions and underlying dynamics, with computation above 1 kHz. Whole-body tracking experiments in simulation and on hardware demonstrate collision avoidance involving the robot body and external obstacles, joint limits, and center-of-mass stability constraints. The authors state that the method remains consistent with the current contact mode and tracking objectives, minimally restricting policy capabilities when constraints are active.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ConstrainedMimic，用于在人形机器人强化学习运动跟踪策略中实时执行约束。该框架结合全身运动学与动力学、操作空间控制和控制障碍函数，可对运动学参考动作及底层动力学施加运行时约束，并以高于1 kHz的频率计算。仿真和硬件上的全身动作跟踪实验展示了对机器人自身及外部障碍物的碰撞规避、关节限位和质心稳定约束。作者称，该方法与当前接触模式和跟踪目标保持一致，在约束生效时对策略能力的限制较小。

sections.text:
Unlike singles, humanoid table tennis doubles requires teammates to strike in strict alternation while sharing a confined workspace. Rapid repositioning can compromise striking accuracy, while uncoordinated teammate movements introduce collision risks. We present PingpongDuo, a hierarchical framework for agile humanoid doubles with safe team coordination.

At the team level, a planner jointly selects positioning targets and uses learned risk estimates to filter risky proposals, preferentially preserving the current striker's target. At the individual level, separate footwork and striking skills combine agile movement with precise racket control.

The skills are guided by human motion references, including footwork collected from human doubles play, and trained from states produced by one another to support rapid transitions. A racket-arm residual further refines strikes after movement using return feedback from a simulator calibrated with real ball-flight and contact measurements.

In simulation, PingpongDuo improves the ball-return success rate by 13.2% over the state-of-the-art baseline, while achieving approximately 2 cm positioning error during clearance.

In real-world experiments, a robot completes a 2.15 m clearance-and-recovery cycle in 2.4 s with a peak speed of 2.23 m/s, while two robots sustain more than 10 consecutive strikes in strict alternation.

summary.en: The paper introduces PingpongDuo, a hierarchical framework for humanoid table-tennis doubles that supports rapid movement and safe coordination in a confined space. A team planner jointly selects positioning targets and filters risky proposals using learned risk estimates, preferentially preserving the current striker’s target. Individual footwork and striking skills are trained with human motion references. In simulation, the system improves ball-return success by 13.2% over a state-of-the-art baseline and achieves about 2 cm positioning error during clearance. In real-world experiments, a robot completes a 2.15 m clearance-and-recovery cycle in 2.4 s at a peak speed of 2.23 m/s, while two robots sustain over 10 alternating strikes.
summary.zh: 论文提出 PingpongDuo，一种用于人形机器人乒乓球双打的分层框架，目标是在狭小场地中实现快速移动与安全协作。团队规划器共同选择站位目标，并利用学习得到的风险估计筛除高风险方案，优先保留当前击球者的目标；个体层将步法与击球技能结合，并以人类动作参考训练。仿真中，相较先进基线，回球成功率提高13.2%，避让时站位误差约2厘米。真实实验中，机器人以峰值2.23米/秒完成2.15米避让与恢复周期，用时2.4秒；两台机器人连续交替击球超过10次。

sections.text:
This paper presents $S^3$-Nav, a structured spatial-semantic decision-making framework for language-guided robot navigation under partial observability.

Rather than assuming a complete environment representation in advance, $S^3$-Nav incrementally constructs persistent spatial-semantic state while exposing only a capacity-controlled, task-conditioned view to the high-level policy.

This separation decouples what the robot must retain from what the policy needs to inspect, allowing decision complexity to be controlled without discarding grounded evidence required for subsequent reasoning and validation.

High-level navigation outputs remain provisional and are independently grounded and validated against persistent semantic evidence and current geometric observations before physical execution or task termination.

Evaluations across multiple environments and object- and relation-goal tasks demonstrate that separating persistent state, decision-facing evidence, and execution authority improves closed-loop navigation reliability while reducing policy reasoning cost.

summary.en: The paper presents S³-Nav, a structured spatial-semantic decision framework for language-guided robot navigation under partial observability. Instead of assuming a complete environment representation, it incrementally builds persistent spatial-semantic state and exposes a capacity-controlled, task-conditioned view to the high-level policy. This separates information the robot must retain from evidence the policy needs to inspect. Navigation outputs remain provisional until independently grounded and validated against persistent semantic evidence and current geometric observations, before execution or task termination. Evaluations across multiple environments and object- and relation-goal tasks show that this separation improves closed-loop navigation reliability while reducing policy reasoning cost.
summary.zh: 论文提出 S³-Nav，一种面向部分可观测环境中语言引导机器人导航的结构化空间语义决策框架。它不预设完整环境表示，而是逐步建立持久的空间语义状态，同时向高层策略提供受容量控制、与任务相关的视图，以区分需要保留的信息和策略需要查看的证据。导航输出在执行或结束任务前，须依据持久语义证据和当前几何观测独立完成落地核验。作者在多个环境以及物体目标、关系目标任务上的评估显示，分离持久状态、决策证据和执行权限可提高闭环导航可靠性并降低策略推理成本。

sections.text:
Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated whole-body interaction with the physical world, yet collecting robot demonstrations at scale remains costly.

Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, but existing egocentric human supervision often omits locomotion and posture, while embodiment differences and controller dynamics hinder accurate end-effector execution.

We introduce HumanVerse, a 500-hour dataset of open-world human loco-manipulation pairing egocentric video with synchronized body and hand motion. Our human-to-humanoid pipeline aligns camera viewpoints and arm appearance, and refines motion references and controller inputs offline to reduce end-effector errors while preserving whole-body coordination.

We validate the pipeline through zero-shot transfer to Unitree G1 on representative whole-body manipulation and long-range loco-manipulation tasks, without target-task robot demonstrations.

Building on this pipeline, we develop $\lambda_0$, a humanoid foundation model for whole-body loco-manipulation, with robot-aligned human demonstrations providing supervision for mid-training.

Increasing whole-body human data consistently improves downstream task progress. $\lambda_0$ achieves 90.0% success on SIMPLE and 62.5% across real-world loco-manipulation tasks. We expect this study to guide scalable whole-body human data collection toward humanoid foundation models for richer interaction with the physical world.

Homepage: https://lambdahumanoid.github.io/

summary.en: The paper introduces HumanVerse, a 500-hour open-world dataset pairing egocentric video with synchronized body and hand motion, and a human-to-humanoid pipeline that refines motion references and controller inputs offline. The authors report zero-shot transfer to Unitree G1 on representative tasks without target-task robot demonstrations. They also present λ₀, a humanoid foundation model supervised with robot-aligned human demonstrations, and report that more whole-body human data improves downstream task progress, with the stated success rates on SIMPLE and real-world tasks.

sections.text:
Integrating world models into Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) has emerged as a promising direction, enabling policies to anticipate future dynamics beyond reactive observation-to-action mapping.

However, existing approaches vary simultaneously in their world representations, integration paradigms, and policy backbones, making it difficult to determine what truly matters for effective world model integration.

To disentangle these factors, we categorize existing efforts into four representative paradigms, namely Implicit Future Alignment, Explicit Future Query, MoT Future Expert, and External World Predictor.

We instantiate each within a unified framework and systematically evaluate these paradigms with diverse world representations and policy backbones across in-domain, out-of-domain, long-horizon, dynamic, few-shot, and real-world settings.

Our study yields four main findings: 1) world representation effectiveness is paradigm-dependent, whereas 2D semantic representations offer robust, cross-paradigm gains; 2) no single paradigm is universally optimal, yet the decoupled MoT Future Expert offers competitive overall performance, particularly in OOD robustness; 3) world modeling consistently benefits policies built on standard VLMs, while decoupled designs exhibit greater compatibility with pretrained VLAs; and 4) world modeling improves performance over action-only baselines across multiple settings, with notable gains on long-horizon and dynamic tasks.

Project page and video demonstrations are available at https://dylanmqs.github.io/WM-in-VLAs/.

summary.en: The study groups world-model integration in vision-language-action models into four paradigms and evaluates them in a unified framework across representations, policy backbones, and multiple settings, including real-world tasks. The authors report that representation effectiveness depends on the paradigm, while 2D semantic representations provide robust gains across paradigms. No paradigm is universally best, but the decoupled MoT Future Expert is competitive overall, particularly for out-of-domain robustness. World modeling improves on action-only baselines, with notable reported gains in long-horizon and dynamic tasks.

sections.text:
Human demonstrations are today used largely for pretraining vision-language-action models, with little ability to use the same data for target-embodiment or task-oriented training, which scalable deployment of robots in industrial and general environments depends on.

A human demonstration recorded on a simple and scalable device such as a mobile phone can serve as post-training data for a robot whose body differs in structure and capability from the human who recorded it. This is made possible not by retargeting the hand's motion but the object's.

A capture yields a body-free record: the object's pose over time, its contact intervals, and a reconstructed 3D object with provenance.

Any robot, given as a URDF and a short descriptor, is solved against that record and scored in simulation against the demonstrated object motion as ground truth: the human-to-simulation leg of human-to-simulation-to-robot transfer, measured per robot.

Each (robot, episode) pair gets one outcome: pass, failure with a named mode, or refusal, with its reason, before any motion.

The method runs as a working system over a growing collection; the set analysed here is a sample of it: 42 captures solved on 8 robots, 157 pairs, of which 31.2% pass, 52.2% fail, 14.0% are refused and 2.5% are unauditable (kinematic feasibility, +/-50 mm / +/-15 deg, in simulation).

Refusals held up: every pair the checks refuse on stored evidence yet ran anyway failed (13 of 13; 5 on a body whose public model welds its hand).A description file could not be shown to screen a robot: its outcomes were barely more predictable than guessing. No policy has yet been trained on the record.

The record decides what a robot may post-train on; whether the policy then works on the real robot is the simulation-to-robot question, answered downstream.

summary.en: The method turns human demonstrations into body-free records of object pose, contact intervals, and reconstructed 3D objects, then evaluates each robot against demonstrated object motion in simulation. The authors report results for a sample of captures and robot-episode pairs, classified as pass, failure, refusal, or unauditable. Refusal checks held up against stored evidence, while a robot description file was barely more predictive than guessing. The abstract states that no policy has yet been trained on these records; whether a policy works on a real robot remains a downstream question.
summary.zh: 论文提出将人类示范中的物体运动而非手部动作作为机器人后训练依据：从手机等设备记录物体随时间的姿态、接触区间和带来源信息的三维重建，再针对给定机器人在仿真中评估其对示范物体运动的匹配。作者报告，在所分析的样本中，涵盖42次采集、8台机器人及157组配对，配对结果包括通过、失败、拒绝及无法审计；拒绝检查在存储证据上有效，但机器人说明文件难以筛选结果。摘要明确说明尚未基于该记录训练策略，真实机器人效果仍待后续验证。

sections.text:
World action models (WAMs) jointly predict future visual states and robot actions, but processing dense future-frame tokens incurs substantial inference latency. We propose CF-Prune, a training-free framework for pruning future-frame tokens in pretrained WAMs.

Our key insight is that future visual predictions support action generation and therefore need not preserve every visual detail required for high-fidelity video synthesis.

CF-Prune combines instruction and action attention to identify task-relevant tokens during the initial denoising forward pass, even when future-frame and action representations remain highly noisy. An entropy-based phase identification mechanism further retains dense computation during precision phases to mitigate pruning-induced performance degradation.

Experiments on RoboLab, RoboCasa, and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate consistent inference speedups. At a 35% pruning ratio, CF-Prune achieves average speedups of 1.19-1.27x while improving task success rates.

At a 50% pruning ratio, it achieves 1.29-1.33x average speedups on both simulation benchmarks, with overall success rates within 1.0 percentage point of the baseline.

summary.en: The paper proposes CF-Prune, a training-free method for pruning future-frame visual tokens in pretrained world action models to reduce inference latency. It combines instruction and action attention to select task-relevant tokens and uses entropy-based phase identification to retain dense computation during precision-sensitive phases. Experiments on RoboLab, RoboCasa, and real-world manipulation tasks are reported to show inference speedups. At the stated pruning ratios, the authors report improved task success at 35% pruning and simulation-benchmark success within 1.0 percentage point of baseline at 50% pruning.
summary.zh: 论文提出无需训练的 CF-Prune，用于剪枝预训练世界动作模型中的未来帧视觉 token，以降低推理延迟。方法结合指令注意力与动作注意力识别任务相关 token，并用基于熵的阶段识别机制，在精度敏感阶段保留密集计算。作者报告，在 RoboLab、RoboCasa 仿真基准及真实世界操作任务上的实验显示，该方法可加速推理；剪枝比例为35%时，平均加速且任务成功率提高，比例为50%时，两个仿真基准的成功率与基线相差不超过摘要所述范围。

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are gaining attention in autonomous driving, inheriting commonsense priors from large language models (LLMs) and widening the navigation interface from a fixed command set to free-form natural-language instructions.

However, this open-ended interface exposes a new vulnerability surface: an inattentive driver may issue instructions that are unsafe given the current scene, and a malicious user may issue dangerous ones on purpose. We present the first benchmark suite that evaluates navigation following and conflict awareness together, along with adversarial robustness.

Existing VLAs fall short on both: SimLingo completes no language-instructed lane change in closed loop, and all models degrade sharply under conflicting signals.

We propose SafeDriveVLA, the first driving VLA that （1） explicitly predicts a three-level navigation-compliance mode to decouple conflict reasoning from action generation, and （2） uses navigation-conditioned world model dreaming to inform this prediction.

Unlike prior world models that roll out expert or planned actions, ours dreams of strictly following the navigation signal, showing when following is safe.

SafeDriveVLA reaches 88.16 Driving Score (DS) and 68.64% Success Rate (SR) on Bench2Drive, lifts closed-loop language following by 49.3% and reduces collisions under unsafe instructions from 60 to 38 compared to the best SimLingo variant. Video demonstrations are available on our project page.

summary.en: The paper introduces SafeDriveVLA for evaluating and handling navigation following and scene conflicts in autonomous-driving VLAs. It predicts a three-level navigation-compliance mode and uses world-model rollouts that assume strict adherence to the navigation signal to help assess safety. The authors report a score of 88.16 and a 68.64% success rate on Bench2Drive. Compared with the best SimLingo variant, closed-loop language following improves by 49.3%, while collisions under unsafe instructions fall from 60 to 38.
summary.zh: 论文提出 SafeDriveVLA，用于评估并处理自动驾驶 VLA 的导航指令跟随与场景冲突。该方法预测三级导航遵从模式，并通过假设严格执行导航信号的世界模型想象来辅助判断其是否安全。作者报告，该模型在 Bench2Drive 上取得 88.16 驾驶分和 68.64% 成功率；相较最佳 SimLingo 变体，闭环语言指令跟随提升 49.3%，不安全指令下碰撞次数从 60 降至 38。

sections.text:
Coding agents can construct executable programs and revise them through feedback, offering a foundation for embodied control without target-task fine-tuning. Through a programmatic robot interface, the agent observes the scene, executes control programs, and adapts them to the resulting physical state, serving as the closed-loop policy.

However, this within-episode adaptation does not automatically preserve experience across scenes. Our trajectory analysis shows that agents spend interaction and inference budgets establishing effective operations and identifying their preconditions, while fresh agents cannot reuse these discoveries.

This motivates EmbodiedEvo, a self-evolving coding agent that distills physical feedback into reusable code Skills and diagnostic Lessons. Experience is acquired on one Playground scene per task, then frozen for independent agents in unseen scenes, without updating model weights.

On RoboDojo-Sim, EmbodiedEvo achieves an average score of 44.48 and a success rate of 37.82\%, surpassing all officially verified results. Paired tests show the largest gains on memory-dependent tasks and successful reuse of coordinated procedures, while fine contact control remains difficult.

Experience from stronger models also improves weaker executors: Astra's experience raises Sol and Luna's success rates by 8.86 and 5.50 percentage points over no experience. Compared with raw interaction history, Skills and Lessons achieve comparable task performance at 53.0\% lower execution cost.

summary.en: EmbodiedEvo turns physical feedback from robot interactions into reusable code Skills and diagnostic Lessons for independent agents in unseen scenes, without changing model weights. On RoboDojo-Sim, the authors report an average score of 44.48 and a 37.82% success rate. Paired tests show the largest gains on memory-dependent tasks, while fine contact control remains difficult. Experience from Astra raises Sol’s and Luna’s success rates by 8.86 and 5.50 percentage points. Skills and Lessons achieve comparable task performance to raw interaction history at 53.0% lower execution cost.
summary.zh: 论文提出 EmbodiedEvo，使编码智能体把机器人交互中的物理反馈整理为可复用的代码技能和诊断经验，并供未见场景中的独立智能体使用；模型权重保持不变。在 RoboDojo-Sim 上，作者报告平均得分 44.48、成功率 37.82%，并称配对测试中记忆依赖任务提升最大，但精细接触控制仍困难。较强模型 Astra 的经验使 Sol 和 Luna 的成功率分别提高 8.86 和 5.50 个百分点；技能与经验在任务表现相近时，比原始交互历史降低 53.0% 执行成本。

sections.text:
Robots navigating open-world, human-centered environments must look beyond prebuilt high-fidelity maps and leverage navigational aids embedded in their surroundings, particularly, signs.

To advance sign-guided visual navigation, we introduce SiGNgapore, an interactive, multimodal dataset designed to benchmark sign-guided multi-step navigational decision-making.

SiGNgapore covers diverse public spaces in Singapore, including shopping malls, public transportation hubs, and hospitals, featuring multi-floor, multi-building layouts and indoor-outdoor transitions. It consists of 56 long-horizon navigation missions and 456 scenes, each containing a navigational sign and its surrounding environment.

We provide synchronized RGB, depth, IMU, and odometry data for each scene. We additionally provide the layout map and the GPS-aligned scene graph for selected mission sites.

Beyond navigational decision-making, SiGNgapore supports a variety of spatial-semantic reasoning tasks, including navigational sign parsing and visual sign grounding, with the ultimate aim of driving progress in mapless robot navigation.

summary.en: The paper introduces SiGNgapore, an interactive multimodal dataset for benchmarking multi-step navigation decisions guided by signs. It covers public spaces in Singapore, including malls, transit hubs, and hospitals, with multi-floor and multi-building layouts and indoor-outdoor transitions. The dataset contains 56 long-horizon missions and 456 scenes, each with a navigational sign and its surroundings. It provides synchronized RGB, depth, IMU, and odometry data, plus layout maps and GPS-aligned scene graphs for selected sites. Supported tasks include sign parsing and visual sign grounding.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 SiGNgapore，这是用于评测依靠环境标志进行多步导航决策的交互式多模态数据集。数据覆盖新加坡商场、交通枢纽和医院等公共空间，包含多楼层、多建筑布局及室内外转换，共有 56 项长时程导航任务和 456 个场景，每个场景包含导航标志及周边环境。数据提供同步 RGB、深度、IMU 和里程计信息，部分任务地点另有布局地图及 GPS 对齐的场景图，可支持标志解析、视觉标志定位等空间语义任务。

items.title: SiGNgapore - An Interactive Dataset for Sign-based Visual Navigation
