sections.text:
Recent advances in 3D hand-object interaction (HOI) perception have opened new opportunities for learning dexterous robotic skills from human videos. However, existing dexterous imitation learning methods often rely on costly and manually teleoperated robot demonstrations, requiring substantial human effort.

Therefore, we build DEXCAST, a framework that learns dexterous robotic hand control directly from monocular RGB-D videos by leveraging joint HOI reconstructions, without requiring any teleoperation. Furthermore, how to model high-dimensional robotic hand motion and extract temporal context to inform future action generation remains a key challenge.

To this end, we propose a DexHand Motion Perception Module (DMPM) to capture inter-joint coordination and temporal dependencies in compact latent representations that condition our diffusion policy. Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate that DEXCAST achieves exceptional performance across diverse dexterous manipulation tasks.

summary.en: The paper introduces DEXCAST, a framework for learning dexterous robotic hand control directly from monocular RGB-D human videos using joint hand-object interaction reconstructions, without teleoperation. It proposes a DexHand Motion Perception Module (DMPM) that encodes inter-joint coordination and temporal dependencies in compact latent representations, which condition a diffusion policy. The abstract states that extensive real-world experiments show what the authors describe as exceptional performance across diverse dexterous manipulation tasks, but provides no task-level or quantitative results.
summary.zh: 论文提出 DEXCAST，从单目 RGB-D 人类视频中直接学习灵巧机器人手控制，无需遥操作示范；其方法利用联合手—物交互重建。为处理高维手部运动及时间信息，作者设计灵巧手运动感知模块（DMPM），以紧凑潜在表示捕捉关节协调和时间依赖，并用于条件扩散策略。摘要称，广泛的真实世界实验显示，DEXCAST 在多种灵巧操作任务中取得了作者所称的出色表现；摘要未给出具体任务或量化结果。

sections.text:
Achieving human-like dexterous manipulation remains a central challenge in robotics. Learning from human hand-object interaction (HOI) datasets offers a promising pathway to diverse dexterous skills, yet existing physics-based approaches train specialist policies for individual trajectories, thereby limiting skill reuse at scale.

We introduce DexMimic, a generalist dexterous hand-object tracking policy jointly trained across diverse HOI trajectories. Efficient joint training requires allocating each rollout to both an undertrained phase and a starting state that supports continued tracking.

DexMimic realizes this insight through Value-Guided Reset Allocation, which adapts the initialization distribution online to prioritize difficult phases and select reset states with higher expected tracking returns. We further introduce a benchmark spanning training, fine-tuning, and generalization.

Experiments show improved tracking success and training efficiency, faster fine-tuning, and the potential for zero-shot generalization to unseen trajectories and objects; larger training sets further improve efficiency and generalization. Finally, we validate DexMimic on a real-world dexterous manipulation platform.

summary.en: DexMimic is a generalist dexterous hand-object tracking policy jointly trained on diverse human interaction trajectories. Its Value-Guided Reset Allocation method adjusts the initialization distribution online, prioritizing difficult phases and reset states with higher expected tracking returns. The paper also presents a benchmark for training, fine-tuning, and generalization. Experiments are reported to improve tracking success and training efficiency, speed up fine-tuning, and show potential for zero-shot generalization to unseen trajectories and objects. The authors also report validation on a real-world dexterous manipulation platform.
summary.zh: 论文提出 DexMimic，一种跨多条人手—物体交互轨迹联合训练的通用灵巧手追踪策略。其价值引导重置分配方法在线调整初始化分布，优先训练困难阶段，并选择预期追踪回报较高的重置状态；论文还介绍覆盖训练、微调和泛化的基准。实验显示，作者报告该方法提升追踪成功率与训练效率、加快微调，并具有对未见轨迹和物体零样本泛化的潜力；更大的训练集进一步改善效率和泛化。论文最后报告在真实世界灵巧操作平台上进行了验证。

items.title: DexMimic: A Generalist Dexterous Hand-Object Tracking Policy via Value-Guided Reset Allocation

sections.text:
Robotic vacuum cleaners must extend their functionality within tight limits on size, cost, and durability. Deployable linkages with few actuators meet these limits, but their backdrivability makes it difficult to hold a load-bearing posture without continuous motor torque.

We introduce a two-stage deployable linkage that is self-locking, in the sense used for toggle and singularity-based linkages, through its own geometry: at full deployment an internal three-link subchain approaches a collinear, near-singular configuration where the input--output transmission ratio approaches zero, so that plate loads produce a small residual back-driving torque, absorbed by drive-train friction and a lightweight magnetic detent.

A single actuator performs deployment and locking, a passive chassis-mounted trigger releases the lock for retraction, and a second actuator adjusts only the deployment height.

We integrate the mechanism into a commercial robotic vacuum cleaner and validate it through a 100-cycle repeatability test, a quasi-static load test in which the locked plate held 50\,N with the motor de-energized, and 140 pushing-type tidying trials on seven household objects against a commercial arm-equipped vacuum robot under a documented protocol.

We derive the analytical holding condition and discuss its limits as an intermediate design point between passive compliance and articulated manipulation.

summary.en: The paper presents a two-stage deployable linkage for robotic vacuum cleaners that uses a near-singular geometry for self-locking. At full deployment, an internal three-link chain approaches collinearity, driving the transmission ratio toward zero and reducing load-induced back-driving torque, which is absorbed by drivetrain friction and a lightweight magnetic detent. One actuator deploys and locks the linkage; a passive trigger releases it for retraction, while another actuator adjusts deployment height. The authors report integration into a commercial vacuum cleaner, repeatability and quasi-static load tests, and pushing trials on household objects, alongside an analytical holding condition and discussion of design limits.

sections.text:
As the Arctic transitions toward a seasonally ice-free state, capturing the complex morphology of submerged sea ice is crucial for advancing models of ocean-ice-atmosphere heat exchange and monitoring under-ice habitats. Currently, sub-surface ice mapping is predominantly achieved through acoustic sensors such as multibeam sonar.

While sonar provides robust large-scale geometry, it lacks spectral and high-resolution textural information required to record fine morphological features - a critical limitation in under-ice environments, where sparse visual features and degraded sensing conditions challenge the capture of detailed structural and optical surface properties.

We present a benchmark for vision-based under-ice 3D reconstruction using real-world data from the MOSAiC expedition and synthetic data generated in an Unreal Engine-based underwater robotics simulator.

The benchmark evaluates Structure-From-Motion (SfM) and monocular depth estimation, with quantitative comparison enabled through cross-modal registration to upward-looking multibeam sonar.

summary.en: The paper presents a benchmark for vision-based 3D reconstruction beneath sea ice, using real-world data from the MOSAiC expedition and synthetic data from an Unreal Engine-based underwater robotics simulator. It evaluates Structure-From-Motion and monocular depth estimation. Cross-modal registration with upward-looking multibeam sonar enables quantitative comparison. The abstract notes that sonar captures large-scale geometry but lacks the spectral and high-resolution textural information needed to record fine morphological features.
summary.zh: 论文提出一项面向冰下机器人感知的视觉三维重建基准，使用 MOSAiC 探险的真实数据，以及由基于 Unreal Engine 的水下机器人模拟器生成的合成数据。基准评估运动恢复结构（SfM）和单目深度估计，并通过与向上观测的多波束声呐进行跨模态配准，支持定量比较。摘要指出，声呐可提供大尺度几何信息，但缺少记录细微形态所需的光谱和高分辨率纹理信息。

items.title: Benchmarking 3D Reconstruction for Under-Ice Robotic Perception in Arctic Environments

sections.text:
Robot-free collection with handheld interfaces enables scalable acquisition of human demonstrations for policy learning. However, existing handheld interfaces often provide limited intuitive force feedback, making contact-rich demonstration collection challenging for human operators.

To address this, we present FOMI, a force-feedback manipulation interface with a scissor-shaped mechanism, which transmits object interaction forces directly to the operator's hands through actuation links without force sensors. This intuitive force feedback supports real-time action adjustment during robot-free collection of contact-rich demonstrations.

Around FOMI, we build a demonstration collection system that integrates sensor calibration, data acquisition, and synchronization for robot-free collection. By further mapping pose changes and gripper opening of FOMI to robot end-effector poses and gripper commands, the system also supports teleoperation.

Across four contact-rich tasks, FOMI improves collection efficiency by approximately 29% and 18% over the best baselines in robot-free collection and teleoperation, respectively. Demonstrations collected with FOMI in both modes enable policies to perform challenging contact-rich manipulation tasks with high success rates.

summary.en: The paper introduces FOMI, a force-feedback interface for teaching contact-rich manipulation. Its scissor-shaped mechanism transmits object interaction forces to the operator’s hands through actuation links without force sensors. The accompanying system supports robot-free demonstration collection and teleoperation. Across four contact-rich tasks, the authors report collection-efficiency improvements of approximately 29% and 18% over the best baselines for robot-free collection and teleoperation, respectively. Policies trained on demonstrations from both modes reportedly achieve high success rates.

Reliable recognition of accessibility-critical objects (e.g., audible pedestrian signals, door-activation buttons, and handrails) is essential for assistive navigation technologies that support safe, independent mobility for blind and low-vision (BLV) users.

Yet these categories are underrepresented in existing large-scale vision datasets, and the few datasets that include them suffer from limited class coverage, inconsistent annotations, and poor diversity.

We introduce NavAble, a large-scale dataset spanning 11 accessibility-critical object classes, combining 41K curated open-source images with 8K newly collected, densely annotated real-world images.

To extend scale and diversity, we develop a synthetic data generation pipeline that renders high-fidelity 3D assets across 37 environments under diverse styles and viewpoints, yielding 452K frames with rich ground-truth annotations from 565 assets.

The pipeline minimizes manual effort by combining automated web image crawling, VLM-based filtering, SAM 3D-based asset generation, and convenient camera trajectory configuration, enabling large-scale data generation at a diversity unattainable through manual collection.

Experiments show that fine-tuning existing segmentation models on the NavAble Dataset achieves reliable accessibility-object segmentation (>80% mIoU on our held-out test set).We also demonstrate the effectiveness of synthetic data augmentation, which yields up to +3.5 mIoU over real-world-only fine-tuning.

Beyond benchmark evaluation, validation on egocentric data from two mobility-assistive robots demonstrates improved perception reliability in real-world navigation scenarios. Together, NavAble establishes a scalable foundation for BLV navigation perception, directly addressing the data scarcity and embodiment gaps.

The dataset and pipeline are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/NavAble/NeurIPS_2026_BLV.

The dataset covers 11 object classes and combines curated open-source images with newly collected, densely annotated real-world images. Its pipeline renders 3D assets across varied environments, styles, and viewpoints to generate annotated frames. Experiments report over 80% mIoU on a held-out test set after fine-tuning segmentation models, and up to 3.5 mIoU improvement from synthetic augmentation over real-world-only fine-tuning. Egocentric data from two assistive robots is also used for validation.

Visual loco-manipulation of arbitrary in-the-wild objects requires accurate end-effector (EE) control and a generalizable understanding of the scene from visual inputs (eg, RGB-D images).Existing imitation and sim2real methods jointly learn both these aspects via monolithic end-to-end learning and are thus hard to scale.

In this work, we bring to bear the best tools for each of these problems -- large vision models for generalizable scene understanding and simulated training for accurate EE control -- leading to an overall modular loco-manipulation system that exhibits strong generalization.

Our core technical innovation is HERO, an accurate residual-aware EE tracking policy made possible by combining classical robotics with machine learning. It uses a) inverse kinematics to convert residual end-effector targets into reference trajectories, b) a learned neural forward model for accurate forward kinematics, and c) goal adjustment and replanning.

Together, these innovations reduce the end-effector tracking error to 2.44cm, outperforming the strongest prior method by 5.5x. Our overall system operates in diverse real-world environments, from offices to coffee shops, where the robot reliably grasps various everyday objects (eg, mugs, apples, toys) on surfaces ranging from 43cm to 92cm in height.

Systematic modular and end-to-end tests demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed design. We believe our advances open up new ways of training humanoids to interact with daily objects. Project page: https://hero-humanoid.github.io/

Transferring robotic skills from simulation to reality requires task knowledge that remains usable across differences in perception, dynamics, and embodiment. We introduce Skill2Real, an agentic policy framework that learns executable skills through a shared application programming interface (API).

A Proposer-Verifier-Governor (PVG) loop uses privileged simulation evidence to diagnose outcomes and validate updates, while keeping learned skills grounded in public observations and API semantics. The Cerebellum first acquires local manipulation skills; the Brain then learns task-level composition with the Cerebellum frozen.

Both memories transfer to the real robot without task-policy fine-tuning or skill-memory updates. As GPT-5.6 Sol learns skills on LIBERO-90, evaluating each frozen checkpoint with GPT-6 Astra raises LIBERO-Pro Long success from 2.0% to 56.3%, without training on Pro Long.

Independent Robosuite training reaches 85.1% and 89.4% mean success with Sol and Opus 5 across seven tasks, respectively. Frozen Sol-trained LIBERO-90 skills achieve 78.75% mean completion across four real-world manipulation tasks with Astra.

Removing the Verifier or Governor during LIBERO-90 training lowers final Pro Long success by 17.3 and 13.3 percentage points, respectively. These results support learning and transferring a hierarchy of executable skills through a common robot interface.

Mobile Manipulation (MoMa) is a cornerstone of autonomous robotic systems, yet real-world fine-tuning remains a formidable challenge because of high-dimensional action spaces and intricate coupling between heterogeneous modules.

In this paper, we propose HiRe-MoMa (Hierarchical Residual Mobile Manipulation), a systematic framework for stable and sample-efficient real-world fine-tuning of complex MoMa systems. At its core, HiRe-MoMa adopts a Hierarchical Residual Architecture that fine-tunes a frozen base policy.

A Policy-Agnostic Residual learns additive corrections atop the base policy, while Hierarchical Decoupling splits the residual into mobile-base and manipulator-arm heads with unidirectional conditioning, mitigating gradient interference and aligning corrections with the platform's physical hierarchy.

To improve sample efficiency in data-expensive real-world settings, we propose Expert-Guided Value Alignment, which leverages sparse human interventions with under 20% training coverage to reshape the critic's value landscape, effectively guiding autonomous exploration through expert priors.

Extensive real-world experiments on the TIAGo++ platform demonstrate that HiRe-MoMa consistently enhances task performance with only around 30 minutes of online interaction, regardless of the base policy architecture.

To our knowledge, this is among the first frameworks to enable efficient on-robot fine-tuning for mobile manipulation in the real world, providing a practical paradigm for deploying complex robotic systems in dynamic, human-centric environments. Further details can be found on our project website: https://hire-moma.github.io/

sections.text:
Whole-body mobile manipulation suffers from two fundamental challenges: inherent motion heterogeneity across locomotion, arm, and hand modules, and progressive error accumulation over long-horizon multi-stage tasks. Existing teleoperation platforms also lack integrated dexterous tactile sensing to support coordinated whole-body decision-making.

This paper presents RoboSpan, a high-DoF whole-body teleoperation and demonstration platform, and the Hierarchical Modular Framework (HMF) for learning modular coordination policies.

HMF functionally decouples the 29-DoF action space into fine hand manipulation, arm pose adjustment, and mobile-base spatial configuration branches, and introduces the Coordinated Modular Embodied Transformer (COMET) with inter-modular cross-attention to enable dynamic information exchange and action coordination.

Vision-language model driven hierarchical task decomposition structurally suppresses temporal error propagation, while a full-palm 2D tactile representation encodes distributed contact signals for cross-module tactile empowerment.

Experiments on a physical 29-DoF robot demonstrate that the proposed method achieves over 20\% higher task success rate than mainstream baselines across a range of long-horizon whole-body tasks, markedly improving stability and robustness in contact-rich manipulation.

summary.en: The paper presents RoboSpan, a whole-body teleoperation and demonstration platform, and HMF, a hierarchical framework for learning modular coordination policies. HMF divides the 29-degree-of-freedom action space into hand, arm, and mobile-base branches, coordinating them with COMET cross-attention. It also uses vision-language-model-driven task decomposition and a full-palm 2D tactile representation. Experiments on a physical 29-DoF robot report task success rates over 20% higher than mainstream baselines across long-horizon tasks, with improved stability and robustness in contact-rich manipulation.

sections.text:
Existing robot policy memories typically evolve with observation sequences, implicitly treating each update as the same amount of physical time. Yet identical observation histories can span different durations and require different actions, exposing physical time as a missing dimension of policy memory.

We introduce Temporal Flow Policy (TFP), which learns memory dynamics to retain past events and evolve the memory state over measured time intervals. Observations and prior memory determine the content and time scales of each transition; elapsed time determines how far the state advances.

TFP conditions diffusion and flow-matching policies through this memory state and is trained with their native imitation objectives. We evaluate TFP with Diffusion Policy and $\pi_{0.5}$ through controlled comparisons of memory designs. These experiments show that successful timing depends on both measured intervals and retained history.

TFP achieves higher average success than the recurrent and state-space memories we equip with the same intervals and than a variant that feeds the interval to a learned gate. Memory readouts recover the time since an event and motion information after occlusion.

Changing the supplied intervals systematically delays or advances actions, linking time inputs to behavior. Real-robot tasks requiring timing or memory, together with LIBERO evaluations, demonstrate benefits in physical and general manipulation.

These results suggest viewing robot memory not as stored observation history, but as a state that retains past events and evolves with physical time.

summary.en: The paper introduces Temporal Flow Policy (TFP), which evolves robot policy memory according to measured time intervals while retaining past events. The memory conditions diffusion and flow-matching policies, trained with their native imitation objectives. Comparisons with Diffusion Policy and π0.5, including real-robot tasks and LIBERO evaluations, report higher average success than recurrent and state-space memories given the same intervals, and than a learned-gate variant. Memory readouts recover event timing and motion after occlusion, while changing supplied intervals systematically advances or delays actions.
summary.zh: 本文提出时间流策略 TFP，使机器人策略记忆根据测得的时间间隔演化，同时保留过去事件。该记忆用于条件化扩散策略和流匹配策略，并通过各自的模仿学习目标训练。作者在 Diffusion Policy、π0.5、真实机器人任务及 LIBERO 评估中进行比较，报告 TFP 的平均成功率高于使用相同时间间隔的循环与状态空间记忆，以及将间隔输入学习门控的变体。记忆读出可恢复事件发生时间和遮挡后的运动信息；改变输入间隔会系统性地提前或延后动作。

items.title: Physical Time as a Missing Dimension of Robot Policy Memory Dynamics

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are a promising paradigm for field robotics, but their deployment is bottlenecked by strict edge SWaP-C constraints. Compression techniques such as quantization, distillation, and pruning are well-established for LLMs and VLMs. Pruning, however, remains particularly underexplored for VLA models.

We surprisingly find that pruning VLA models yields drastic performance degradation and increased safety violations. Through spectral analysis, we identify structural properties of VLA weights that help explain this fragility.

Based on this insight, we introduce GLUESTICK, a post-pruning recovery method that restores much of the original model's capability while preserving sparsity benefits. GLUESTICK computes a one-time corrective term by interpolating between the dense and pruned models in weight space.

At inference, each pruned layer applies this correction to recover lost performance with minimal overhead. Our approach requires no additional training and is agnostic to the pruning algorithm.

Across diverse VLA architectures and domains, GLUESTICK recovers up to 100% of the success rate and restores safety to near-dense levels, while saving up to 5 GB of memory and achieving up to 1.75x speedup. Additional material can be found at: https://gluestick-vla.github.io/

summary.en: The paper reports that pruning vision-language-action models can sharply reduce performance and increase safety violations, and uses spectral analysis to examine structural factors behind this fragility. It introduces GLUESTICK, which computes a one-time correction by interpolating between dense and pruned weights and applies it during inference. The authors say it needs no additional training and is pruning-algorithm agnostic. Across evaluated architectures and domains, they report recovering up to 100% of success rate, near-dense safety, memory savings up to 5 GB, and speedups up to 1.75x.

items.title: Don't Run with Scissors: Pruning Breaks VLA Models but They Can Be Recovered

sections.text:
Differentiable reinforcement learning shows strong promise for robot policy learning, but its application to legged locomotion has remained limited to blind walking or simulated 2D tasks.

Extending it to end-to-end visual obstacle avoidance is challenging because hard collision constraints and early termination upon contact corrupt first-order gradients, trapping optimizers in local minima.

We present E2DRL, which addresses this with a soft differentiable obstacle-interaction formulation: penetration penalties across multiple body keypoints with velocity-conditioned stop-gradient shaping to provide the first-order training signals for 3D obstacle avoidance.

To realize a deployable perception-control system, a privileged teacher trained via Soft Analytic Policy Optimization (SAPO) in a differentiable simulator is distilled into a recurrent depth-based student via DAgger, then blended with a base locomotion policy using a terrain-aware gating module for deployment.

In simulation, E2DRL achieves higher sample efficiency than PPO and demonstrates superior velocity-tracking performance and 3D obstacle-avoidance capability compared with both PPO and Duality-based DCBF NMPC.

We present the first sim-to-real validation of end-to-end differentiable RL for 3D obstacle avoidance on a Unitree Go2 in static and dynamic environments.

summary.en: The paper presents E2DRL for end-to-end visual 3D obstacle avoidance in quadruped robots. Its differentiable obstacle interaction uses penetration penalties over multiple body keypoints and velocity-conditioned stop-gradient shaping to provide first-order training signals. A privileged teacher trained in a differentiable simulator is distilled through DAgger into a recurrent depth-based student, then combined with a base locomotion policy for deployment. In simulation, the authors report better sample efficiency than PPO and stronger velocity tracking and 3D avoidance than PPO and Duality-based DCBF NMPC. They also report sim-to-real validation on a Unitree Go2 in static and dynamic environments.
summary.zh: 论文提出 E2DRL，用于四足机器人在三维环境中进行端到端视觉避障。方法以可微的障碍物交互形式处理碰撞约束，通过多个身体关键点的穿透惩罚和依赖速度的停止梯度塑形提供一阶训练信号。系统先在可微仿真器中训练特权教师，再通过 DAgger 将其蒸馏为基于深度信息的循环学生策略，并与基础运动策略结合部署。仿真结果显示其样本效率高于 PPO，速度跟踪和三维避障表现优于 PPO 与基于对偶性的 DCBF NMPC。作者还报告了在 Unitree Go2 静态和动态环境中的仿真到真实验证。

sections.text:
Humanoid policies trained in simulation can transfer qualitatively to hardware while failing to transfer the force interactions learned during training, compromising torque efficiency, load regulation, and robustness to impacts. This failure can arise from actuator sim-to-real gaps because forces depend on actuator torques.

We introduce Contact-UAN, a residual world model that preserves a simulator's physics priors while correcting actuator dynamics to align simulated rollouts with recorded hardware rollouts.

For humanoid motion with contact, this requires contact-consistent replay: if hardware playback in simulation begins with misaligned contact wrenches, the residual model learns to correct reset artifacts rather than actuator discrepancies.

Using only onboard proprioception, Contact-UAN infers the simulator-side stance-foot pose needed to initialize replay with consistent contact forces.

We show that a UAN trained on 6.5 minutes of real-world walking data generalizes to tasks that benefit from accurate force and impulse regulation and produces policies that transfer seamlessly to the real world, yielding 20% lower running torque, 43% lower force-tracking error, extreme compliance, accurate impedance control, and dynamic, robust jumps.

summary.en: The paper introduces Contact-UAN, a residual world model that adjusts actuator dynamics so simulated rollouts align with hardware recordings while retaining the simulator's physics priors. The authors note that contact playback with mismatched initial contact forces can make the model learn reset artifacts instead of actuator differences. Contact-UAN uses onboard proprioception to infer the simulator-side stance-foot pose for contact-consistent replay. They report that a UAN trained on 6.5 minutes of real walking data generalizes to tasks requiring force and impulse regulation, and describe real-world policy transfer with lower running torque and force-tracking error, compliance, impedance control, and dynamic jumps.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Contact-UAN，一种残差世界模型，用于修正仿真中的执行器动力学，使仿真轨迹与真实硬件记录对齐，同时保留仿真器的物理先验。作者指出，接触动作回放若从不一致的接触力开始，模型可能学到重置误差而非执行器差异；因此该方法仅用机载本体感知估计仿真侧支撑脚姿态，以初始化接触力一致的回放。作者报告，使用6.5分钟真实步行数据训练的 UAN 可泛化到需要力与冲量调节的任务，并称策略能迁移到真实世界，呈现更低运行扭矩和力跟踪误差、柔顺性、阻抗控制及动态跳跃表现。

sections.text:
Surface navigation on the Moon is subject to extreme illumination contrast and deployment-time perceptual disturbances. While modular navigation pipelines have long supported planetary rover navigation, robustness is compromised by measurement errors that propagate through hand-engineered components.

End-to-end learned policies are an alternative approach to navigation, which maps observations directly to control actions without intermediate components. Vision-language-action models, in particular, have driven significant breakthroughs in robotics and autonomous vehicle research.

By leveraging internet-scale vision-language pretraining, these models can be exploited for their commonsense reasoning and visual understanding to provide robust generalization with limited task-specific data. However, their applicability and performance have yet to be characterized for lunar surface operations.

In this study, we design a vision-language-action policy for autonomous lunar rover docking and characterize its performance relative to a modular navigation pipeline. We develop a scalable training framework that generates safety-aware expert demonstrations in a high-fidelity lunar simulation environment.

In closed-loop evaluations, our policy performs competitively relative to the modular baseline under perceptual disturbances unseen during training. To address the tradeoff between compute consumption and closed-loop safety, the policy adapts its execution horizon by determining how far the rover may safely travel in open loop.

Adaptive-horizon execution reduces inference frequency while limiting hazard-contact rates relative to fixed horizons in the evaluated scenarios.

summary.en: The paper develops an end-to-end vision-language-action policy for autonomous lunar rover docking and compares it with a modular navigation pipeline. Its scalable training framework generates safety-aware expert demonstrations in a high-fidelity lunar simulation. In closed-loop evaluations, the policy performs competitively against the modular baseline under perceptual disturbances absent from training. To balance compute use and closed-loop safety, it adapts its execution horizon by estimating how far the rover can safely travel open loop. The authors report that, in evaluated scenarios, adaptive horizons reduce inference frequency while limiting hazard-contact rates relative to fixed horizons.

sections.text:
We present KinoGen, a framework that synthesizes customizable humanoid loco-manipulation references through kinematically grounded video generation.

KinoGen conditions a pretrained video generator on calibrated renders of the target robot and object in a simulated task instance and recovers the reference by fitting the same models to the generated two-view video, so that the reference lies in the robot configuration space by construction without a human body proxy or retargeting.

Body, hand, and object priors initialize the reconstruction, and direct optimization against cross-view evidence refines it. Since an edited keyframe is simply another rendered state, a user can prescribe a goal object pose, regenerate the video around the edited keyframe, and obtain a reference that satisfies the pose exactly.

Across eight loco-manipulation tasks, KinoGen yields lower penetration and foot skating than video-based baselines and preserves over 90% of annotated contacts, and its customized references satisfy every prescribed target with substantially less penetration than direct interpolation.

Tracking policies trained on the synthesized references are deployed on a Unitree G1 humanoid with dexterous hands. Project webpage: https://kinogen-humanoid.github.io/.

summary.en: KinoGen synthesizes customizable humanoid loco-manipulation references through kinematically grounded video generation. It conditions a pretrained video generator on simulated renders of the target robot and object, then fits those models to generated two-view video to recover references in the robot’s configuration space without a human proxy or retargeting. Users can edit a keyframe to prescribe an object pose. Across eight tasks, the authors report reduced penetration and foot skating versus video baselines, preservation of over 90% of annotated contacts, and successful tracking-policy deployment on a Unitree G1.

sections.text:
Registering two captures of the same indoor space taken at different times underpins persistent spatial memory for robots and AR systems, yet the realistic version of this task is egocentric and its most scalable form is RGB-only. Head-mounted cameras yield blurry, fast-moving, partially overlapping views from which dense geometry is hard to recover.

Classical registration leans on exactly the clean point clouds this setting lacks, while learned scene-graph methods require a pre-built or annotated graph and a trained matcher that we find brittle under egocentric data. We take a different route, using a pretrained vision-language model as the source of both scene understanding and cross-scan matching.

Our method, PROSE (Prompted Scene rEgistration), lifts each RGB sequence into an object-level 3D scene graph using off-the-shelf foundation models for geometry, segmentation, and language, then prompts the same VLM to match object instances across the two RGB sequences.

To make this matching tractable and reliable, we leverage object heights as a prior and verify each proposed match with a paired same/different query, then solve for the rigid transform by hypothesizing a candidate per matched object and selecting the one with the strongest geometric consensus.

PROSE adds no learned parameters and requires no depth sensor, training, or annotated graph.

On the egocentric Aria Digital Twin and Aria Everyday Activities benchmarks, it outperforms both geometric and learned scene-graph baselines in registration accuracy, on ground-truth and RGB-reconstructed point clouds alike, and the scene graph it produces transfers directly to downstream tasks.

summary.en: PROSE registers egocentric RGB captures of the same indoor space taken at different times. It uses pretrained vision-language and off-the-shelf models to lift RGB sequences into object-level 3D scene graphs, match instances across sequences, verify candidate matches, and estimate a rigid transform from geometric consensus. The method adds no learned parameters and needs no depth sensor, training, or annotated graph. On two Aria benchmarks, the authors report higher registration accuracy than geometric and learned scene-graph baselines, using both ground-truth and RGB-reconstructed point clouds.
summary.zh: PROSE面向不同时间采集的室内第一人称RGB序列配准，使用预训练视觉语言模型完成场景理解和跨序列物体匹配。方法借助现成模型将序列转换为物体级三维场景图，以物体高度辅助匹配，并通过同异判断核验候选，再依据几何共识求取刚体变换。它不增加学习参数，也不需要深度传感器、训练或标注图。作者报告，在两个Aria基准上，无论使用真值还是RGB重建点云，PROSE的配准准确度均优于几何和学习式场景图基线；生成的场景图可用于下游任务。

sections.text:
Autonomous robots often need to move their camera before they can act: to inspect an object, reveal an occluded region, or obtain a view that responds to a user's intent.

While vision-language navigation translates instructions to base motion and vision-language-action policies map instructions to manipulation actions, vision-language conditioned camera motion remains comparatively underexplored as a first-class action.

We formulate vision-language conditioned camera motion generation: given a current RGB observation and a free-form natural-language intent, predict a relative target camera pose for the next observation.

The challenge is that useful viewpoint changes depend on latent perceptual intent, ranging from coarse spatial moves to fine-grained inspection or occlusion revealing.

To model this structure, we mine multi-intent camera-motion supervision from egocentric video via hindsight labeling, pairing each relative SE（3） target pose with plausible intents and observation-gain descriptions inferred from the reached view.

We propose LIME, a vision-language camera-motion generator that combines an autoregressive observation-gain output with a continuous flow-matching pose head. This design lets the model jointly predict what the next view should reveal while representing multi-hypothesis target views.

Across viewpoint-prediction experiments and downstream robotic tasks, we show that LIME learns intent-conditioned camera motion from passive egocentric video, turning ordinary human recordings into supervision for a reusable active-perception primitive that supports general-purpose viewpoint selection, manipulation, embodied question answering, and mid-distance navigation.

summary.en: LIME predicts a relative target camera pose from a current RGB observation and a free-form natural-language intent, treating camera motion as an action for inspection, revealing occlusions, or responding to a user. The authors mine multi-intent supervision from egocentric video by pairing relative pose targets with plausible intents and descriptions of observation gain. LIME combines an autoregressive observation-gain output with a continuous flow-matching pose head. In viewpoint-prediction experiments and downstream robotic tasks, the authors report learning intent-conditioned camera motion from passive video and supporting several embodied tasks.
summary.zh: LIME研究根据当前RGB观察和自然语言意图生成相机下一步的相对目标位姿，使机器人主动改变视角以检查物体、呈现遮挡区域或响应用户需求。作者从第一人称视频中通过事后标注挖掘多意图相机运动监督，将目标位姿与可能意图及观察增益描述配对。模型结合自回归观察增益输出和连续流匹配位姿头，联合预测新视角应揭示的内容与目标视角。作者称，视角预测实验和下游机器人任务表明，该方法能从被动视频中学习意图条件相机运动，并支持多种具身任务。

sections.text:
When diffusion policies were first introduced, they were expected to recover multi-modal action distributions. However, we find this expectation does not always hold, as diffusion policies often collapse to a single modality even when we guarantee the balance of dataset modalities and exact within-batch symmetry.

Our analysis indicates that independent action-noise pairing contributes to this failure by increasing mixing and crossing among diffusion paths, which can produce averaged denoising responses and suppress modality-specific behavior.

This issue is especially severe in robot planning, where action spaces are dense and low-dimensional, significantly increasing such mixing and crossing.

To alleviate this problem, we propose Immiscible Diffusion Policy, a label-free training-time add-on to diffusion policy that uses action-noise assignment to preserve relatively distinct noise-to-action routes without modifying the policy architecture or inference procedure.

Across five simulated and two real-world humanoid manipulation tasks spanning state, RGB, and point-cloud observations, our method significantly improves the policy's preservation of action modalities while maintaining strong task performance.

It increases the proportion of the non-dominant modality by 6.0x-14.6x across three two-modality tasks and recovers demonstrated modalities that are entirely absent from vanilla policy rollouts on both four-modality tasks.

These results demonstrate that Immiscible Diffusion Policy provides a simple yet robust approach to preserving action multi-modality in general robot learning tasks.

summary.en: The authors report that diffusion policies can collapse to one action mode despite balanced datasets, and attribute this partly to independent action-noise pairing that increases mixing among diffusion paths. Immiscible Diffusion Policy is a label-free training add-on that assigns action noise to keep noise-to-action routes relatively distinct, without changing the policy architecture or inference. Across five simulated and two real-world humanoid manipulation tasks with state, RGB, and point-cloud observations, they report improved modality preservation with strong task performance. The method increases the non-dominant mode share in three two-mode tasks and recovers demonstrated modes absent from vanilla rollouts in two four-mode tasks.
summary.zh: 作者指出，扩散策略即使在数据模态均衡、批次对称时，也可能坍缩到单一动作模态；独立动作噪声配对会加剧扩散路径混合与交叉，进而压制模态特有行为。Immiscible Diffusion Policy是一种无标签训练附加方法，通过分配动作噪声保持噪声到动作路径相对分离，不改变策略架构或推理过程。在五项模拟和两项真实人形机器人操作任务中，涵盖状态、RGB及点云观察，作者报告该方法提升了动作模态保留并维持较强任务表现；在两模态任务中非主导模态比例提升6.0至14.6倍，并在两项四模态任务中恢复基线策略未产生的示范模态。

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) policies fine-tuned on LIBERO are trained and evaluated on the same ten instruction strings, and rewording the instruction changes base OpenVLA's success by -38.0 points. Test-time prompt ensembling, which improves language models, does not recover this loss in any setting we ran.

Paraphrase consensus (the medoid action over K paraphrases) costs base OpenVLA 16.8 points when the training instruction is a member. Without it, the medoid of the paraphrases scores -32.4 points relative to the training instruction, and confidence-based selection scores -28.0.

The same medoid over samples of one paraphrase improves on greedy decoding but stays -27.6 points below the training instruction, consistent with aggregation reducing variance without removing the bias the paraphrases share. A wrong-instruction probe measures how much of a policy's success depends on the instruction.

Across three policies and four suites, paraphrases cost a policy only where this share is high, and the stronger policies lose a much smaller fraction of it than base OpenVLA.

LoRA post-training on paraphrased instructions reduces the one-paraphrase effect to +2.0 points, against -32.0 for a matched control, reproduces across two seeds and on OpenVLA-OFT, transfers to withheld phrasings, and leaves the policy's reliance on the instruction unchanged.

summary.en: The paper studies instruction reliance and robustness to paraphrasing in vision-language-action policies. On LIBERO, rewording instructions reduced base OpenVLA’s success, and test-time prompt ensembling did not recover the loss. Aggregating actions across paraphrases or selecting by confidence also remained below performance with the training instruction. Across policies and suites, paraphrase effects were associated with instruction reliance. LoRA post-training on paraphrased instructions reduced the reported one-paraphrase effect across two seeds and on OpenVLA-OFT, transferred to withheld phrasings, and left instruction reliance unchanged.
summary.zh: 论文研究视觉语言动作策略对指令改写的依赖与鲁棒性。作者报告，在 LIBERO 上微调并使用相同十条指令训练和评估时，改写指令会降低基础 OpenVLA 的成功表现，测试时提示集成未能恢复损失。对多个释义动作取 medoid 或按置信度选择也未消除与训练指令之间的差距；跨策略和测试套件的结果显示，释义影响与策略对指令的依赖程度相关。对释义指令进行 LoRA 后训练，在两种随机种子及 OpenVLA-OFT 上复现了改善，并迁移到未见措辞，但未改变策略对指令的依赖。

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong potential for general-purpose robotic manipulation, but extending them to bimanual dexterous manipulation introduces a high-dimensional and structured action space.

Existing bimanual VLA policies commonly concatenate right- and left-side arm--hand actions at each control timestep, leaving cross-hand interactions implicit within a single action vector. We introduce Coordi-$\pi$, a structured action representation for bimanual dexterous manipulation.

Coordi-$\pi$ represents the right- and left-side arm--hand actions as individual action tokens and organizes them into an interleaved sequence, explicitly exposing the two sides within the action sequence.

To explicitly encode hand identity and temporal synchronization in this interleaved representation, a learnable hand-identity embedding distinguishes the two sides, while sequence--control-timestep factorized rotary positional encoding (RoPE) separates sequence position from control timestep, allowing actions at the same control timestep to share a temporal coordinate while retaining distinct sequence positions.

Across all five bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks in DexJoCo, Coordi-$\pi$ achieves state-of-the-art performance under both \textit{rand-obj} and \textit{rand-full}, improving the average success rate over $\pi_{0.5}$ from 31.9\% to 51.3\% and from 18.3\% to 32.3\%, respectively.

Coordi-$\pi$ also consistently outperforms $\pi_{0.5}$ across four real-world bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks.

summary.en: The paper introduces Coordi-π, a structured action representation for bimanual dexterous manipulation. It encodes right- and left-side arm-hand actions as separate tokens in an interleaved sequence, with a learnable hand-identity embedding and factorized rotary positional encoding for sequence position and control-timestep synchronization. Across five DexJoCo tasks, the authors report better performance than π0.5 under both rand-obj and rand-full settings, with higher average success rates. They also report consistent outperformance of π0.5 across four real-world bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Coordi-π，用于双手灵巧操作的结构化动作表示。该方法将左右侧臂手动作分别表示为动作 token，并交错排列；可学习的手身份嵌入区分两侧，按序列与控制时间步分解的 RoPE 则编码位置和时间同步。在 DexJoCo 的五项任务中，作者报告其在 rand-obj 和 rand-full 设置下均优于 π0.5，平均成功率分别从 31.9% 提高到 51.3%、从 18.3% 提高到 32.3%。作者还报告，该方法在四项真实世界双手灵巧操作任务中持续优于 π0.5。

items.title: Coordi-pi: Coordination-Aware Dual-Hand Action Representation for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation

sections.text:
A wearable assistive robot must continuously estimate terrain, locomotion mode, gait phase, and walking speed. These quantities are commonly addressed by separate, terrain-specific models, with datasets rarely collected under a common protocol.

This paper presents a visuo-inertial framework that connects these estimates through a causal pipeline using a chest-mounted camera and four lower-limb inertial measurement units (IMUs).Anticipatory Terrain Perception (ATP) classifies incoming terrain with 96.3% accuracy and anticipates terrain transitions by 1.46 s on average.

Terrain-Aware Locomotion Mode Identification (TALMI) achieves 93.7% and 98.8% accuracy for its level-ground and stairs experts respectively, with mean transition latencies being below 200 ms.

The relevant TALMI posterior is retained as a Probabilistic Locomotion Context (PLC) vector and provided to a shared Gait Kinematic Encoder (GKE), which supports 50-Hz bilateral gait-phase estimation and 2-Hz walking-speed estimation.

Leave-one-subject-out evaluation yields gait-phase RMSEs of 1.75%, 2.97%, and 4.55% for level walking, stair ascent, and stair descent respectively while estimating speed over 3.5-5.5 km/h with a RMSE of 0.218 km/h.

All inertial sensing based models use sensor-fused Euler angles as input rather than raw accelerometer and gyroscope signals, reducing dependence on sensor mounting variation.

summary.en: The paper presents Tread, a visuo-inertial framework for estimating terrain, locomotion mode, gait phase, and walking speed for wearable robotics. It uses a chest-mounted camera and four lower-limb inertial measurement units in a causal pipeline: terrain and locomotion context estimates are passed to a shared gait encoder. In leave-one-subject-out evaluation, the authors report gait-phase errors for level walking, stair ascent, and stair descent, and walking-speed error over a specified speed range. The inertial models use sensor-fused Euler angles rather than raw accelerometer and gyroscope signals to reduce sensitivity to sensor mounting variation.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Tread，一种结合胸前摄像头与四个下肢惯性测量单元的可穿戴机器人视觉惯性框架，以因果流程估计地形、运动模式、步态相位和行走速度。框架先识别前方地形和运动模式，再将概率运动情境提供给共享步态编码器。留一受试者评估报告了平地行走、上楼和下楼的步态相位误差，以及特定速度范围内的速度估计误差。惯性模型使用传感器融合的欧拉角，而非原始加速度计和陀螺仪信号，以降低对传感器安装差异的依赖。

items.title: Tread: A Visuo-Inertial Framework for Terrain and Locomotion Context-Aware Gait-Phase and Speed Estimation in Wearable Robotics

sections.text:
Monocular videos of human manipulation provide abundant dexterous demonstrations, yet reconstructing hand-object interaction from a single view and transferring it to robot hands remain difficult, limiting their direct use for robot execution.

Prior methods either require task-specific RL training, limiting scalability, or assume clean motion-capture trajectories and thus cannot operate directly on video. We present OmniHOI, a pipeline that turns an RGB video of hand-object interaction into an interaction-faithful trajectory on dexterous hands.

The key idea is to enforce physical consistency using the evidence available at each stage: image evidence during reconstruction, contact geometry during retargeting, and dynamics during physics-in-the-loop refinement.

Each stage optimizes the corresponding representation directly, correcting errors before they propagate downstream or must be absorbed by a learned policy. Across 150 motion-capture trajectories transferred to each of five dexterous hands with 6 to 22 DoF, we achieve 39-89% success, compared with at most 31% for prior transfer methods.

On 60 monocular video clips, we achieve 53% success, compared with 28% for the best prior video-to-robot pipeline. Its trajectories also execute on a real bimanual robot across diverse tasks.

summary.en: The paper presents OmniHOI, a pipeline that converts monocular RGB videos of human hand-object interaction into trajectories for dexterous hands. It applies image evidence during reconstruction, contact geometry during retargeting, and dynamics during physics-in-the-loop refinement, correcting representations stage by stage. The authors report higher success than prior transfer methods when transferring motion-capture trajectories to five dexterous hands, and higher success than the best prior video-to-robot pipeline on monocular video clips. They also report that the resulting trajectories execute on a real bimanual robot across diverse tasks.
summary.zh: 论文提出 OmniHOI，将单目 RGB 人手物体交互视频转换为适用于灵巧手的交互轨迹。方法在重建阶段利用图像证据，在重定向阶段利用接触几何，并在物理仿真闭环优化阶段考虑动力学，以逐阶段修正误差。作者报告，在动作捕捉轨迹迁移至五种灵巧手的评估中，成功率高于既有迁移方法；在单目视频片段上也高于既有视频到机器人的流程。论文还报告，这些轨迹可在真实双手机器人上执行多种任务。

sections.text:
State-of-the-art visuomotor policies are increasingly capable of executing complex tasks, yet can fail during deployment in ways they cannot predict or recover from on their own.

Improving their performance and robustness typically requires collecting more data, retraining, or modifying the policy architecture, all of which are time- and resource-intensive in practice. We instead propose an offline-trained monitoring-and-intervention framework that improves a policy during deployment using only black-box query access.

From a limited set of labeled on-policy rollouts, we learn a policy-conditioned liveness value that measures the nominal policy's progress toward task completion; we additionally train a compact latent world model using these rollouts together with play data. At deployment, the liveness value continuously monitors execution.

When it detects a loss of progress, a short-horizon planner searches the world model for corrective actions using the same value as its planning objective, after which control returns to the nominal policy.

We evaluate our method on the LIBERO-Goal task suite and on a Franka Panda manipulator, using the vision-language-action model $\pi_{0.5}$ and a diffusion policy as nominal policies, and demonstrate significant improvements in task success rates, while supporting real-time control.

Additional results and videos are available on the project website (https://policy-improvement-wm.pages.dev/).

summary.en: The paper proposes an offline-trained monitoring and intervention framework for improving visuomotor policies at deployment through black-box query access. It learns a policy-conditioned liveness value from a limited set of labeled on-policy rollouts and trains a compact latent world model using those rollouts and play data. When progress is lost, a short-horizon planner searches for corrective actions, then returns control to the nominal policy. Evaluations on LIBERO-Goal and a Franka Panda manipulator report significant task success improvements and real-time control support.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种部署时监测与干预框架，旨在仅凭黑盒查询改善既有视觉运动策略，无需部署期间重新训练。方法从少量带标签的在策略轨迹学习衡量任务进展的活性值，并结合这些轨迹与 play 数据训练紧凑潜在世界模型。检测到进展停滞时，短时域规划器在模型中搜索纠正动作，之后控制权返回原策略。作者在 LIBERO-Goal 任务套件及 Franka Panda 机械臂上评估，使用两种名义策略，并报告任务成功率显著提升且支持实时控制。

sections.text:
Robot actions are inherently embodiment-specific and only weakly aligned with image-space visual changes, limiting their effectiveness as conditioning signals for robot world models.

In contrast, visual tracks provide an embodiment-agnostic representation of how task-relevant points move through a scene, offering dense image-space guidance for accurate and spatially precise future video prediction.

Building on this observation, we propose TrAct, a world-model-based robot decision-making framework that uses visual tracks as an intermediate interface between control and prediction.

TrAct consists of three components: a Vision-Language-Action-and-Track model (VLAT) that jointly predicts candidate actions and corresponding visual tracks from the current observation and language instruction; a track-conditioned world model (TWM) that predicts future visual outcomes conditioned on the proposed tracks; and a vision-language reward model (VLAC) that scores the predicted outcomes.

At inference time, VLAT generates candidate action-track pairs, TWM rolls out their visual consequences, and VLAC selects the track whose predicted outcome best satisfies the instruction; the action paired with the selected track is then executed by the robot.

Experiments on the proposed LIBERO-INTEGRAL benchmark and real-world Franka manipulation show that TrAct improves success rates from 27% to 55% in simulation and from 49% to 76% on real-world tasks compared with the strong VLA baseline $\pi_{0.5}$.Furthermore, TWM consistently improves video prediction quality over the action-conditioned world model (AWM).

These results demonstrate that visual tracks provide an effective shared interface between robot control and visual prediction, enabling more accurate world modeling and stronger robot generalization.

summary.en: TrAct uses visual tracks as an intermediate interface between robot control and visual prediction. Its components jointly propose candidate actions and tracks, predict future visual outcomes conditioned on tracks, and score those outcomes against instructions. At inference, the robot executes the action paired with the selected track. On the proposed LIBERO-INTEGRAL simulation benchmark and real-world Franka manipulation tasks, the authors report success rates rising from 27% to 55% and from 49% to 76%, respectively, compared with a strong VLA baseline. Track-conditioned prediction also improves video quality over an action-conditioned world model.

sections.text:
A central challenge in mobile manipulation is preserving multiple plausible action modes while remaining reactive during execution. For example, grasping a bottle in a cluttered scene can be achieved through multiple physically feasible base-arm motion plans.

Deterministic VLA policies trained with $L_1$ regression are efficient, but they tend to average across valid modes and may produce physically invalid actions.

Diffusion-based generative policies can better represent multimodal action distributions, yet their proposals may be weakly constrained when generated from pure noise, and iterative sampling can increase inference cost.

Action chunking helps amortize inference, but it also introduces partially open-loop execution, allowing small mismatches to accumulate into drift. We present MobiGuide, a generative VLA model for efficient mobile manipulation, where action generation is guided by a structured trajectory vocabulary.

Constructed from expert demonstrations, this vocabulary encodes plausible whole-body motion patterns and provides structured priors for feasible action generation.

Given the current observation and instruction, MobiGuide locally refines these reference trajectories into context-compatible action proposals and selects the most suitable trajectory for execution. This preserves multimodal action candidates while keeping generation constrained around feasible expert-like motion modes.

To mitigate chunk-induced drift, we further introduce a lightweight residual correction module that performs high-frequency, per-step adjustments during rollout. Across diverse mobile manipulation tasks, MobiGuide improves success and stability under execution disturbances while maintaining low-latency inference.

summary.en: MobiGuide is a generative vision-language-action model for mobile manipulation that guides action generation with a structured trajectory vocabulary derived from expert demonstrations. Given an observation and instruction, it locally refines reference trajectories into context-compatible proposals and selects one for execution, preserving multiple candidates while constraining them around plausible motion patterns. A lightweight residual correction module makes per-step adjustments to mitigate drift from chunked execution. The authors report improved success and stability under execution disturbances across diverse mobile manipulation tasks, while maintaining low-latency inference.

sections.text:
Rapid progress in AI agents and robotics makes it a matter of the near future that humans are served by a team of robots. Such a team will receive several goals at once, each specified in whatever form is convenient for the human, such as a category name, a photo, or a spoken description.

Existing benchmarks study multi-agent, multi-modal, and multi-object goal navigation in isolation, and a benchmark that places all three in one episode is missing. To fill this gap, we introduce HM3D-M3.

A team of K agents starts at distributed locations in a photorealistic indoor scene and searches for an unordered set of M object goals, each given as an open-vocabulary category, an instance image, or an instance description.

HM3D-M3 provides 1,000 validation episodes over 3,926 goals from 379 open-vocabulary categories, 100K observation-assignment training samples, and two team-level metrics, goal-level SR and makespan-normalized SPL. We further contribute two baselines.

HiGA is a trained hierarchical goal assigner on top of a frozen open-vocabulary navigation policy, and LaViRA-M3 is a training-free team of VLM agents with shared mapping and progress analysis. Adapted multi-robot and zero-shot methods reach 16--27% SR, while our baselines reach 38--41% with complementary strengths and distinct failure modes.

Furthermore, we deploy LaViRA-M3 on a heterogeneous three-robot team. Project page: https://robo-lavira.github.io/hm3d-m3/

summary.en: The paper introduces HM3D-M3, a benchmark that evaluates multi-agent, multi-modal, multi-object goal navigation within one episode. Agents start at distributed locations in an indoor scene and search for goals specified by category, instance image, or description. The benchmark includes validation episodes, training samples, team-level metrics, and two baselines, HiGA and LaViRA-M3. The authors report higher success rates for their baselines than for adapted methods on the benchmark, and describe deploying LaViRA-M3 on a heterogeneous three-robot team.

items.title: HM3D-M3: A Benchmark for Multi-Agent, Multi-Modal, Multi-Object Goal Navigation

sections.text:
Real-time volumetric mapping for a planning robot is dominated by the cost of integrating and storing information at the finest resolution, yet only a small fraction of any map ever lies on or near a path the planner actually considers.

We exploit this with a tiered-resolution mapping mechanism that integrates LiDAR into a single map structure at two resolutions simultaneously: fine inside a corridor around the robot's current plan, and coarse everywhere else.

As opposed to traditional navigation pipelines where path planning uses the mapping result and provides no feedback, we propose a feedback loop where planning also informs mapping to dynamically integrate information at different leaf resolutions.

Across two real-world teleoperated datasets, replayed and scored offline against an independent full-resolution map, the tiered maps are 13-15x smaller and require 6-8x less integration CPU time than a uniform fine map, while producing paths at a similar cost per meter as the ones generated from fine resolution maps on both scenarios.

A uniform coarse map reaches the same size savings but its path quality collapses (+210% cost per meter) on the harder scenario, because it over-discretizes terrain the robot must traverse. Tiering approximates the coarse map's cheapness without its failure mode.

summary.en: The paper proposes tiered-resolution volumetric mapping that integrates LiDAR at fine resolution near the robot’s current planned corridor and at coarse resolution elsewhere. Planning also feeds back into mapping to guide resolution choices. In offline replay and scoring on two real-world teleoperated datasets, using an independent full-resolution map for comparison, the tiered maps were smaller and required less integration CPU time while producing paths with similar cost per meter to fine-resolution maps. A uniform coarse map achieved comparable size savings but sharply worsened path cost in the harder scenario.
summary.zh: 论文提出分层分辨率体积地图，将 LiDAR 数据同时以两种分辨率整合：机器人当前规划路径周围采用高分辨率，其余区域采用低分辨率；规划结果还会反馈并影响地图整合。在两组真实世界遥操作数据集上，作者离线回放并与独立全分辨率地图比较。分层地图体积更小、整合所需 CPU 时间更少，生成路径的单位距离代价与精细地图相近。均匀粗分辨率地图虽有相同的体积节省，但在较难场景中路径代价明显上升。

items.title: Tiered-Resolution Volumetric Mapping for Real-Time Simultaneous Planning and Mapping on Natural Outdoor Environments

sections.text:
Recent advances in robot learning have driven rapid progress in humanoid control, enabling increasingly agile behaviors in the real world.

However, humanoid control networks are typically obtained through conventional training procedures, while comparatively little attention has been given to directly modeling the distribution of their learned weights and generating functional networks in weight space.

In this work, we investigate whether high-performing humanoid control networks can be generatively modeled directly through their weights. We adopt a latent diffusion framework that couples a linear autoencoder with a Diffusion Transformer.

The autoencoder compresses actor network parameters into a compact latent space, and the Diffusion Transformer models the distribution of these latents.

Trained on networks collected from reinforcement learning for the Unitree G1 robot, our approach generates deployable networks that perform various motions in the real world, including walking, dancing, and spin kick. Beyond generation, we further study the learned weight space to better understand the structure captured by these humanoid control networks.

We identify a structural principle in the first-layer weights that consistently reflects the robot's kinematic prior.

Notably, this kinematic prior emerges under both Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Imitation Learning (IL) training, suggesting that it is not specific to a particular optimization process but may instead reflect common knowledge associated with humanoid embodiment.

Together, these results demonstrate the feasibility of generative modeling in humanoid network weight space, while providing initial insights into the information encoded by their learned weights. Additional results are available on our project website: https://humanoid-weight-diffusion.github.io/

summary.en: The paper investigates generating humanoid control networks directly in weight space using a latent diffusion framework built from a linear autoencoder and a Diffusion Transformer. Trained on reinforcement-learning networks for the Unitree G1, the approach generates networks that the authors report can be deployed in the real world for motions including walking, dancing, and a spin kick. Their analysis identifies a pattern in first-layer weights that reflects the robot’s kinematic prior. The authors observe this under both reinforcement-learning and imitation-learning training and present it as an initial insight into information encoded in learned weights.
summary.zh: 论文研究能否直接在权重空间生成高性能人形机器人控制网络，并采用由线性自编码器和扩散 Transformer 组成的潜在扩散框架。模型使用 Unitree G1 机器人的强化学习网络训练，作者报告生成的网络可部署于现实世界，执行行走、跳舞和旋踢等动作。对权重空间的分析还发现，首层权重中的一种结构原则反映了机器人的运动学先验；该现象在强化学习和模仿学习训练下均出现。作者据此讨论人形网络权重中编码的信息。

sections.text:
Foundation models are driving a paradigm shift in robotic intelligence, moving beyond low-level action prediction to goal-directed orchestration of data collection, model training, task planning, and real-world execution.

We characterize this emerging paradigm as an agentic robots, in which agents reason over human instructions, interact with robotic environments, rectify execution errors autonomously, and dynamically adjust operational strategies. Although this field develops fast, current studies are not well connected.

Researchers have no consistent view of how to combine different agentic functions into a complete robot system. This paper provides a unified overview of existing research on agentic robots. We first trace the development from robot policies to agentic systems, covering vision-language-action models, world models, and world-action models.

We then clarify the definition and scope of agentic robots and organize existing research into seventeen categories across four functional domains: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness.

Across these domains, we examine how agents shape model learning and robot decisions, collect and curate robot data, construct worlds, tasks, and tests for learning and evaluation, and organize capabilities for robot use. Finally, we discuss open challenges and outline directions for future research.

Looking forward, we hope this work contributes to a clearer understanding of agentic robots and supports new approaches to making them more capable, reliable, and adaptive.

summary.en: This overview surveys agentic robots, in which foundation-model-based agents coordinate data collection, model training, task planning, and real-world execution around goals. It traces development from robot policies to agentic systems, covering vision-language-action models, world models, and world-action models, and clarifies the field’s scope. The authors organize prior work into seventeen categories across four domains: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness. They discuss how these areas shape learning and decisions, curate robot data, build worlds and evaluations, and organize capabilities, then outline open challenges and future directions.
summary.zh: 这篇综述梳理以基础模型为驱动、能够围绕目标协调数据收集、模型训练、任务规划和现实执行的“智能体机器人”研究。作者回顾从机器人策略到智能体系统的发展，涉及视觉语言动作模型、世界模型和世界动作模型，并界定该领域的范围。论文将研究归纳为模型、数据、环境和执行框架四个功能领域下的十七类，讨论各领域如何支持学习、决策、数据整理、环境构建和能力组织，最后提出开放挑战与未来方向。

sections.text:
Multimodal models and agents have emerged to enable AI systems to learn from and interact with the real world more like humans by integrating information across multiple modalities.

However, enabling multimodal agents to continually acquire useful information from complex, heterogeneous multimodal data remains a significant challenge as they move toward long-horizon tasks and lifelong settings.

Addressing this challenge requires effective memory mechanisms that can maintain continuity across sessions, adapt to changing users and environments, and refine memory-management policies through accumulated experience.

We introduce a two-axis analytical framework for multimodal agent memory structured around two key questions: how multimodal information is formed and represented (Axis I, Formation and Representation), and how its management adapts with accumulated experience (Axis II, Memory Management).

Axis I, Formation and Representation, characterizes what information is retained and how it is encoded (e.g., modality-specific embeddings, textual and structured records, latent and parametric representations) to support subsequent reasoning and action.

Axis II, Memory Management, distinguishes three tiers: T1 Static Memory reuses fixed memory; T2 Dynamic Memory updates memory through a stable policy; and T3 Self-Evolving Memory updates memory through an evolving policy.

Based on this framework, we synthesize recurring design patterns and derive principles for balancing source fidelity with abstraction, maintaining temporal validity and provenance, grounding memory use in recoverable evidence, and evolving memory policies over time.

Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and potential future directions for the memory mechanism of multimodal agents.

items.title: Seeing, Maintaining, and Learning: The Evolution of Multimodal Agent Memory

Automating biological laboratories requires robots to perform dexterous tool interactions under realistic visual conditions while handling dynamic experimental phenomena, presenting significant challenges for robotic manipulation.

To enable systematic evaluation under these conditions, we introduce DexBioLab, a simulation benchmark and framework for dexterous manipulation in realistic biological laboratory environments.

DexBioLab comprises 14 tasks across 4 robot embodiments, spanning functional tool use, precision manipulation, language-conditioned visual grounding, and instrument operation. We introduce controllable dynamic experimental phenomena, including flames, vapor, and bubbles, to capture the evolving visual conditions of laboratory procedures.

To further enhance environmental realism, we develop a hybrid rendering pipeline that integrates interactive simulated foreground objects with Gaussian-splatting backgrounds reconstructed from 6 real laboratory scenes.

For efficient large-scale data generation and evaluation, we further build a parallel simulation framework on top of mjlab, proposing Parallel Finite-State Machine (PFSM) and integrating batched rendering with decoupled trajectory replay for demonstration generation and model-independent closed-loop policy evaluation.

Our evaluation reveals substantial variation in policy performance across tasks, exposing distinct strengths and weaknesses of current manipulation policies. Real-world experiments further demonstrate a reduced sim-to-real gap, supporting the validity of AutoBio+ for realistic manipulation evaluation.

Supplementary materials are available at https://cumulusalpha.github.io/DexBioLabWebPage.

sections.text:
Certifiable optimization provides global optimality guarantees for non-convex state estimation in robotics. However, under severe physical sensing degeneracy, convex Semidefinite Programming relaxations solved via Interior-Point Methods suffer from rank expansion, rendering direct semidefinite solving and spectral rounding algebraically invalid.

In this paper, we establish a universal candidate-driven dual certification framework that resolves this challenge without incurring rank expansion.

First, from an epigraph perspective, we prove that while sensing degeneracy expands the primal optimal set into a flat equi-cost face, cost tightness and multiplier recovery remain strictly intact, enabling global verification without direct semidefinite solving.

Second, we propose an observability-aware local search using solution remapping, coupled with a closed-form dual multiplier recovery scheme that executes in sub-microsecond latency.

Third, we derive a model-specific adaptive dual safety threshold parameterized by the minimum non-zero eigenvalue of the observable Hessian and uneradicated residual leakage, preventing false rejections of optimal candidates under weak observability. We validate our universal framework with robust registration under degenerate measurements.

summary.en: The paper addresses global optimality certification for robotic state estimation under severe sensing degeneracy, where semidefinite relaxations may undergo rank expansion. The authors propose a candidate-driven dual certification framework. They state that degeneracy can flatten the primal optimal set while preserving cost tightness and multiplier recovery, enabling verification without direct semidefinite solving. The method combines observability-aware local search, solution remapping, closed-form multiplier recovery, and an adaptive safety threshold. It is validated on robust registration with degenerate measurements.
summary.zh: 论文研究严重观测退化下机器人状态估计的全局最优性认证问题，指出半正定松弛可能出现秩扩张，使直接求解和谱舍入失效。作者提出候选驱动的对偶认证框架，称退化虽会使原问题最优解形成等代价平面，但代价紧性与乘子恢复仍可用于全局验证。方法结合观测性感知局部搜索、解映射、闭式乘子恢复及自适应安全阈值，并以退化测量下的鲁棒配准验证框架。

sections.text:
Robot task planning in real-world environments requires mapping abstract natural language instructions to executable action sequences under long horizons and complex constraints. While large language models (LLMs) provide strong commonsense reasoning, they often fail to generate reliable and feasible plans.

In contrast, symbolic planners ensure feasibility and optimality but require well-specified goals and cannot directly interpret high-level human intent.We formulate robot task planning as learning to generate verifiable subgoals in the Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL), bridging language understanding and symbolic planning.

To address the challenges of sparse and noisy supervision, we propose Trace-Guided Policy Optimization (TGPO), a reinforcement learning framework that improves structured subgoal generation through (i) verifier-grounded rewards, (ii) external correction of intermediate reasoning traces, and (iii) constrained policy updates that incorporate corrected traces into training.We evaluate TGPO on large-scale household planning tasks with long horizons, abstract instructions, and complex constraints.

TGPO significantly outperforms prompting-based and reinforcement learning baselines, with the largest gains on abstract tasks. Furthermore, TGPO integrates naturally with symbolic planners and language-conditioned executors, enabling robust long-horizon planning and combinatorial generalization in realistic environments.

summary.en: The paper formulates robot task planning as generating verifiable PDDL subgoals, connecting natural language understanding with symbolic planning. To address sparse and noisy supervision, it introduces TGPO, a reinforcement learning framework using verifier-grounded rewards, external correction of intermediate reasoning traces, and constrained policy updates that incorporate corrected traces. On large-scale household planning tasks, the authors report that TGPO outperforms prompting-based and reinforcement learning baselines, with the largest gains on abstract tasks. They also describe integration with symbolic planners and language-conditioned executors.

sections.text:
Robotic disassembly of end-of-life (EoL) products requires robots to accommodate product variation, follow prerequisite sequences, and approach components precisely for contact-rich manipulation.

Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) provides a practical path for adaptation, but limited and costly disassembly data cannot capture the distribution shifts arising from changing environments and product uncertainties.

The policy's own rollouts record its approach attempts, and human corrections demonstrate recovery from its errors, but turning these experiences into better policy performance remains challenging.

We introduce PACER, a Process-Aware Correction and Evidence Reweighting framework that learns from these experiences through SFT, using progress toward the target and each trace's source and outcome to weight valid action chunks in the native supervised action loss.

PACER trains one policy per weighting setting and selects one of the resulting policies through held-out validation. We evaluate PACER on UR5e motherboard disassembly across five component classes, where it achieves 87/100 successful approach-and-handoff trials on the held-out benchmark, compared with 54/100 for vanilla post-SFT.

summary.en: The paper introduces PACER, a supervised fine-tuning framework that uses a policy’s own rollout attempts and human corrections to improve robotic disassembly. It weights valid action chunks according to progress, trace source, and outcome, then selects among policies using held-out validation. On UR5e motherboard disassembly across five component classes, the authors report 87 successful approach-and-handoff trials out of 100 on a held-out benchmark, compared with 54 for vanilla post-SFT.
summary.zh: 论文提出 PACER，一种利用机器人策略自身执行轨迹和人类纠正来改进拆解操作的监督微调框架。它依据任务进展、轨迹来源和结果，对有效动作片段加权，并通过留出验证选择策略。作者在 UR5e 主板拆解的五类组件任务上评估，留出基准中 100 次接近并交接试验有 87 次成功；作为比较，普通监督微调后策略为 54 次。

sections.text:
Tactile sensing is becoming central to robust, adaptive, and dexterous robotic manipulation. Beyond its traditional role in contact detection and reactive control, touch is increasingly used to learn transferable representations, condition manipulation policies, and support embodied physical reasoning.

Yet existing surveys largely emphasize tactile hardware and perception, leaving the rapid shift toward learning-based tactile manipulation insufficiently synthesized. This paper reviews tactile-guided skill learning from a learning-centric perspective, organized by the functional role of touch across the learning and control pipeline.

We examine tactile representation and policy learning, tactile foundation models, predictive and adaptive control, and generalization across objects, tasks, sensors, embodiments, and simulation-to-real transfer.

Across these directions, we identify common design principles and remaining challenges in learning transferable physical representations, integrating semantic reasoning with contact-level control, and scaling tactile learning across heterogeneous data and hardware.

Finally, we outline emerging directions toward tactile foundation and world models that can predict, reason about, and adapt physical interactions. Together, this review characterizes the transition of touch from a task-specific feedback signal toward a core modality for general-purpose embodied intelligence.

summary.en: This review surveys tactile-guided robotic skill learning from a learning-centered perspective. It covers tactile representations and policies, foundation models, predictive and adaptive control, and generalization across objects, tasks, sensors, embodiments, and simulation-to-real transfer. The authors identify challenges in learning transferable physical representations, combining semantic reasoning with contact-level control, and scaling across varied data and hardware. They also discuss tactile foundation and world models, describing touch as an emerging core modality for embodied intelligence.
